items.body:
Ghost Dubs & The Bug duppy the latter’s cult, isolationist ambient excursion of 2022 with apposite measures of lead-boot trod and atmospheric levity for the hardest-to-please industrial dub freaks.

Selected cuts from ’Sub Zero’ - Kevin Richard Martin’s concerted return to interests in ambient-dub-noise fundamentals - are robustly togged out with bass insulation and Goretextured to the elements for a supremely crushing session that benefits from the biggest speakers you can lay yr mitts on. It catches KRM arguably in his imperial phase, sustaining a tear of substantial gear penned under his own name since ‘Sirens’ (Room 40, 2019) deep into the belly of his sound, to now clasp these chiral aspects of his steez - the supine, sunken, and strongback, stepping - in a deathly bind.

KMR’s key spar and Pressure MVP, Ghost Dubs goes super dank and wide on his half, opening subterranean caverns of space below ‘When I’m Gone’, punctuated only by abandoned ice-breaker clank and timber-shiver chorales, before pushing leagues below into knackered Porter Ricks or Rhythm & Sound terrain on rework of ‘Sorrow’. Martin keeps up his end of the bargain with a sonorous diffusion of ‘Screwed’, all icy plangency and keeling bass recalling aspects of Mika Vainio’s ‘Kilo’, then plumbing guttural crevasses of the spirit on remix of ‘Too Human’.
items._genre: ambient dub / industrial / noise / bass music / experimental electronic
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑是对Kevin Richard Martin 2022年专辑《Sub Zero》的remix再创作，由The Bug和Ghost Dubs两位合作者分别操刀。The Bug一侧延续其标志性的工业dub风格，厚重低频裹挟着冰冷的噪音质感与金属质感的环境声效，将原专辑的氛围推向更具侵略性与压迫感的极端，适合在大功率音响系统上完整呈现。Ghost Dubs则深入地下空间，在When I'm Gone中拓展出广阔的低频洞穴，冰山碰撞般的金属撞击与木质颤抖的声学元素交织，随后在Sorrow的重新编排中沉入极简techno与dubtechno的幽深地带。Martin本人则亲自重混了Screwed与Too Human，前者弥漫着冰冷共鸣与倾斜的低频线条，后者潜入喉音质感的深层裂缝。整张作品在原版氛围基底之上叠加了dub制作中常见的手法——回响、延迟与空间深度，同时保留了ambient、noise与industrial之间的张力平衡，是对原专辑声音宇宙的一次纵深延展。

items.body:
Taking their cues from the 1968 silent film 'Le Révélateur', Berlin-based Hungarian-Transylvanian artist Réka Csiszér (aka VÍS) and Radwan Ghazi Moumneh (aka Jerusalem in My Heart) use synths, voices and various instruments to breathe new life into Philippe Garrel’s iconic work.

If you heard last year's grimly romantic 'Danse des Larmes', Csiszér's second VÍS album and another one-of-a-kind oddity on the always good Heat Crimes label, you might already have an inkling of how good this one's gonna be. The record was made between November 2025 and February of this year between Zurich and Montréal, where Moumneh runs the legendary Hotel2Tango studio, and it's some of the most chilling material we've heard from either artist. The duo first met in 2018 and initially debuted their soundtrack to 'Le Révélateur' live in 2023; the film had been a long-time favorite of Moumneh's, but Csiszér didn't need much convincing - its themes of displacement and disorientation made immediate sense to an artist who'd grown up with an ever-shifting idea of home, born in East Germany before moving to Vienna.

And after performing their free-flowing soundtrack a handful of times, improvising within a set of tight themes, they decided to document the project properly, borrowing a mate's house in Montréal for a few weeks to record the meat and bones. And although the baseline for the album version of the collaboration is the same ("composed through improvisation," they say), it sounds as if the themes have been weathered and lived in a little at this stage. If you've seen the film, you'll realize it's the unique mood - accentuated by Garrel's stark lighting and Michel Fournier's bold black-and-white cinematography - that carries it, and it's this high-contrast, peripatetic motion that Csiszér and Moumneh capture so magically. 

Opening track 'wahid – واحد' suggests darkness ahead with its eerie environmental sounds (creaking gates, crackly vinyl, caged birds), scraped strings and isolated synths that accompany a shot of a couple smoking in a door frame, their silhouettes cut out of the sunlight. But like the film itself, it's the juxtaposition that makes it hit; 'ithnan – اثنان' is almost celestial, an uncanny hymn made from analogue drones and soft-focus wordless voices. And when they shift into grittier territory on 'arba'a – أربعة', a short distorted instrumental that sits alongside a shot of a young boy seemingly torturing a doll, the album's long centerpiece 'khamsa – خمسة' follows it up with Csiszér's most stunning vocal performance, that lifts a long shot of the nomadic family walking down a forest road.

It's minimal but never for dull for even a moment - best viewed alongside Garrel's film for the optimum experience.
items._genre: experimental / ambient / drone / film score / improvisation
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是柏林匈牙利裔特兰西瓦尼亚艺术家VÍS（Réka Csiszér）与Jerusalem in My Heart（Radwan Ghazi Moumneh）为1968年菲利普·加雷尔无声电影《Le Révélateur》创作的原声。两人2023年首次现场演出该配乐，后在蒙特利尔Hotel2Tango工作室将即兴框架正式录制。专辑通过模拟器轰鸣、失焦无词人声、刮擦弦乐与孤立合成器，捕捉影片黑白高对比度影像中的游牧与迷失感。Csiszér的人声在长达数轨的核心曲中达到极为动人的呈现。阿拉伯数字曲目名与表演方式呼应中东文化背景，使作品在跨文化实验层面具有独特深度。建议与原片同步观看以获得最佳体验。

items.body:
Topdown Dialectic’s solo debut bow on False Aralia rounds up over a decade of material in supremely elusive style & pattern - all rug-pulling rhythms and hallucinatory fractals wrapped up with proper, hyperreal frisson. Massive chef’s kiss FFO Vladislav Delay, Beatrice Dillon, Paperclip Minimiser, Purelink, Marc Leclair.

An artist keenly observed since initial gestures on /\\Aught in the early ‘10s, and throughout their cult LP trilogy for Peak Oil during 2018-2021; Topdown Dialectic has become a unique facet of C.21st dub electronics, adored for their grasp of diffused spatio-textural sorcery and wraithlike grooves. Anyone paying close attention to emergent sounds via Peak Oil and its False Aralia offshoot may have guessed at TD’s signature, watermarked imprint on the Borgesian Term EP of late ’25, which can now be confirmed as the work of one and the same Izaak Schlossmann; a photographer and producer patently in possession of heightened proprioceptions and a rewardingly patient approach to lushly dissociative sonification. In other words, he makes some of the sexiest electronic music out there - stuff that genuinely feels like it was made this century - and his latest practically leaves you kissing the sky thru its 80 minutes of lip-biting, skin tingling pressure. 

On 16 tracks timed at exactly 5 minutes each, we’re placed in the presence of suggestive sorcery, eliding unarchived material and jams in a unique ecology of oneiric physics. Never overtly showy or overblown, there’s nevertheless a staggering level of ingenuity and synaesthetic effect to its detailed construction and gaseous fractals resembling the LSD or DMT experience. The label themselves compare its nuance to “the flicker of a candle over a desk of drum machines in a Midwestern basement, or the “first blush of sunlight over a tiny campground as subwoofers creak in the distance”, which proves a perfectly poetic analog to its digitally-smudged refractions and tongue-tip spectral tumescence. 

Ultimately, it’s a singular pleasure to immerse the senses in Topdown Dialectic’s self-contained soundsphere, and never more substantially so than on ‘False LP A’. Longtime enthusiasts will surely recognise his skill in parsing salient aspects of Basic Channel x Rhythm & Sound, and their descendants in Vladislav Delay or Pole, reframing those templates in far more uncertain space with a real animist magick. Each work feels tangibly, ambiguously alive, breathing with dynamics and more voluminous, macro scales, and iridescent with voices and details that commands attentive listeners who will have a field day zoning in/out to its illusive, holographic projections and syncopated chronics.
items._genre: dub techno / experimental electronic / ambient / IDM
items._cn_summary: 这是制作人Izaak Schlossmann化名Topdown Dialectic的首张全长专辑，收录了横跨十余年的未发行素材，以16首各长5分钟的曲目构筑出一个内省的声学生态。作品延续了Basic Channel与Rhythm & Sound系dub电子的脉络，但将其推入更不确定的空间：节奏不断拧紧又松开，织体如气体般弥散，听感接近致幻剂体验中那种呼吸般的膨胀与收缩。评论特别指出其声音设计的层次感——每首作品都像拥有自主生命般动态起伏，细节在全频段中若隐若现。厂牌将其比作中西部地下室中烛光映照鼓机，或是营地清晨低音炮隐约传来的低频嗡鸣，暗示了专辑物理性与冥想性的双重特质。False Aralia作为Peak Oil的支线厂牌延续了小批量实验电子的发行逻辑，整张作品展现出对空间、纹理与时间感的高度控制力。

items.body:
Performed by Balinese gamelan duo KADAPAT and Indonesian singer and musician Nova Ruth Setyaningtyas, 'Ocean Cage' is a live recording of Asiandopeboys latest performance 'Moyang & Seaman', a collaboration with choreographer Siko Setyanto that draws from Japanese Noh theater and Nusantara traditions.

If you've been paying attention, you'll already know that anything with Tianzhuo Chen's name on it is worthy of a closer look. And Chen is in the director's chair on 'Ocean Cage', fusing installation art, choreography, live music and scenography into a brand new Asiandopeboys theatrical extravaganza that's almost predictably ambitious. The show is pegged to a narrative that's inspired by Indonesian whaling traditions and local legends, focusing on three characters that Setyanto interprets to build an allegorical account of displacement and ecological collapse. But the interesting part for those of us who aren't able to check into one of the shows is that the music is gripping even without the visuals; KADAPAT approach gamelan traditions with a refreshing level of irreverence, using electronic instruments as well as the traditional bamboo and metal tools to mash up the timeline, not exactly fusing gamelan elements with far-off templates but rethinking the form in situ. 

Their tonal clusters and rhythmic experiments are aptly meshed with Nova Ruth's powerful vocals, that sail across the soundtrack, sometimes squeezed into an unsettling robotic moan and oftentimes left to soar on its own. She grew up in Java and spent seven years traveling on the solar-powered boat Arka Kinari, a "floating cultural platform to sound the alarm on climate change." So the music sounds as if it's plugged into a reality that gets more stark each year; there's a sense that 'Ocean Cage', although it's steeped in ancient traditions, is being beamed from the future, a warning of where the world is headed if we don't do something immediately. It's beautiful, of course, but it's sobering too.
items._genre: experimental gamelan / contemporary composition / world fusion / electronic
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由巴厘岛佳美兰双人组与印尼歌手Nova Ruth合作录制，是一场融合装置艺术、编舞、现场音乐与舞台美术的剧场演出实况。作品以印尼捕鲸传统和地方传说为叙事线索，由编舞家Siko Setyanto以日本能剧与努山达拉群岛传统为基底进行诠释，聚焦于流离失所与生态崩溃的寓言。音乐层面，佳美兰传统竹制与金属打击乐器与电子手段并置，既非简单嫁接外部模板，也不是传统融合，而是在原有形式内部进行重新思考，调性集群与节奏实验与Nova Ruth充满力量的人声交织，后者有时被压缩成不安的机械呻吟，有时自由舒展。Nova Ruth曾随太阳能船Arka Kinari航行七年，将气候危机的紧迫感注入音乐。整张专辑扎根古老传统，却仿佛来自未来的警示信号，沉静而清醒。

items.body:
Finally, Kompakt issue a true GAS outlier on vinyl for the first time, recorded in 1989 and containing some of Wolfgang Voigt’s earliest and starkest recycling of magisterial Wagner loops, closest to the ends of The Caretaker, Philip Jeck, Kevin Drumm.

One of those releases that has lurked on our shelves since 2008 as a book and CD, ‘November 89’ exists in the margins of Wolfgang Voigt’s GAS canon as its creepiest and most occluded evocation of long walks in the Bavarian forests. While other GAS classics ooze a sort of dappled warmth breaking thru the trees in their widescreen dub techno strolls, you can fully feel the light dying over the horizon and the forest drawing in on this particularly gloomy, hour-long suite. 

As the title suggests, it was mostly, remarkably, made in ’89, back when Voigt was finding his feet between techno, house and indie-pop, and nearly a decade before he co-founded Kompakt with Michael Mayer & Jürgen Paape - by which time he was a full-fledged rave dynamo as Love Inc. and myriad others notable projects. And, in that sense, it can be heard as his ‘Selected Ambient Works 89-95’ - or perhaps more pertinently with SAW II vibes - in his nascent attempt to chase the ambient dragon, which surely endures for its strangely nostalgic, unheimlich qualities.

An educated guess leads us to think the first three were made in ’89, taking in the nightfall scenery of smudged symphonic strings and icy crackle to ‘Der Wald’, plus the muddied bass waltz and spectral pall of ‘Das Moor’, thru the self-evidently titled centrepiece ‘1989-11-01’, bristling with a digitally iridescent dread. ‘Tal 90’ and ‘Nah Und Fern’, which shares its title with the 2008 boxset, were most likely made a little later, and find the wintry doom thawing to the GAS-eous forms we’ve all come to deeply know and adore. 

A true evergreen for deep ambient techno connoisseurs, no less
items._genre: ambient / dark ambient / experimental electronic / dub techno / drone
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑收录了Wolfgang Voigt（GAS）1989年的早期录音，是其首次以黑胶形式正式发行。评论将其定位为GAS作品中最阴暗、最隐蔽的一张，与The Caretaker、Philip Jeck、Kevin Drumm的质感相近。全长约一小时的套曲以瓦格纳式的循环采样为核心，在模糊的交响弦乐、冰裂的颗粒噪声和阴郁的低频氛围中展开森林夜幕的意象。前三首明显创作于1989年，捕捉黄昏光线消逝的瞬间；后两首稍晚完成，逐渐过渡到后来GAS标志性的宽屏dub techno形态。整张专辑呈现Voigt在techno、house与独立流行之间的过渡状态，是其ambient探索的源头之一，被视为对Aphex Twin《Selected Ambient Works》的德式回应。评论来自独立电子音乐平台Boomkat，原作内容详实，具有较高的参考价值。

items.body:
Abstract dub dream-weavers SKRS INTL. & WZRDRY remerge at the behest of Bristol’s Accidental Meetings for a super lush dose of wormholing ambient dance pressure tipped FFO Rezzett, Peak Oil/False Aralia, Second Woman.

‘Orbit Flares’ combines the two Canadian units for the first time in over a decade, naturally reprising an empathic level of vibes in a half hour of music that betrays illusive tekkerz developed over the interim. Any semblance of sharp edges are smudged to a brilliantly psychedelic, polychromatic lustre and laced with disciplined, yet properly wayward rhythms that tumble, buckle and vaporise in fractious delirium. Each new SKRS drop is welcome around ours but, jeez, they really push into their most impressive work here, possibly thanks to wzrdryAV’s synaesthetic suss.

Front to back it feel likes they catch minds/bodies in the split second before going under anaesthesia, and extrude us into pitch-bent helical vortices of plonging dub chords and gooey bass, finding bold new realms of computerised dub suss. Handrails are slippery as fuck, ground melts beneath feet, leaving bodies gyring in space between the weightless dub techno inflections of ‘1.1’, into air-stepping chicanery on ‘1.2’, or glitching like a hair-kissing Vladislav Delay on ‘1.3’. The smeared chords and scudding subs of ‘2.1’ call to mind Second Woman emulating the illusive dub-soul of False Aralia drops, and ‘2.3’ feels like distant rig heard on a Nitrous-induced permo. 

Sheer class for harder to please future dub freaks.
items._genre: ambient dub / experimental electronic / dub techno / glitch
items._cn_summary: 加拿大两组声音实验者时隔十余年再度合作，由布里斯托尔小厂Accidental Meetings发行，半小时音乐呈现高度迷幻的抽象氛围舞曲质感。所有锐利棱角被柔化为多彩光泽，节奏在失控与纪律间反复撕扯，合成器chord与低频在空间中扭曲融化。评论指出作品捕捉了麻醉前最后一瞬的意识状态，将听者抛入螺旋状的失谐dub漩涡，尾段某些段落使人联想到Second Woman或False Aralia式的幽微情绪，也有段落接近Vladislav Delay的碎裂律动处理。整张专辑在模糊的dub techno边界上持续滑动，质感黏稠而致密，节奏结构却始终处于溃散临界点，是面向资深实验电子听众的高密度作品。

items.body:
Oren Ambarchi and Will Guthrie reconvene for a killer, fully tooled-up fusion of organ-esque Leslie vamps, sitar-style twangs and Guthrie's Han Bennink-inspired full kit theatrics - cover art of the year included.

Ambarchi and Guthrie are both so well established by now that they can do their thing completely free from the weight of expectation, and they've been working together for so long that they seem to fully operate on instinct. They know how it goes, they're just able to flex. And this set, recorded by Rabih Beaini and Filippo Samoré at Beaini's own Morphine Raum studio-cum-venue in Berlin before it was mixed and mastered a year later by Joe Talia, might be their best to date.

On the first side, they take it as slow as they like, with Ambarchi using his Leslie setup to transform his guitar into an organ, creating sustained notes that give Guthrie the space he needs to take the lead, landing on half rhythms and skeletal sequences for a moment before shifting to the next. It works like an establishing shot, building tension and making us wait for the pay off.

On the flip, it finally comes; Ambarchi's guitar is reshaped into a machine gun of harsh feedback resonances, angrily bowed into splintered riffs and sitar-like vibrations that shatter across the sonic spectrum. Guthrie works not just to fill in the gaps, but to provide momentum, swinging boldly from hushed pattern rolls to full, explosive jazz freakouts that anticipate Ambarchi's return to the Leslie. When Ambarchi starts plucking at the strings like a man possessed, coaxing out percussive staccato melodies that almost harmonise with Guthrie's cymbal bells, it all starts to slow down into wailing, woodwind-esque bird calls.

Heavy, heady biz from the best of the best...
items._genre: free improvisation / experimental / jazz fusion / drone
items._cn_summary: Oren Ambarchi 与 Will Guthrie 再次合作的专辑，以即兴演奏为核心，将吉他通过 Leslie 旋转喇叭系统转化为类似风琴和西塔琴的声响，与 Guthrie 受 Han Bennink 启发的全鼓组戏剧化打击形成对话。A 面以缓慢铺陈建立张力，Ambarchi 的延音给予 Guthrie 充分空间展开半拍律动与骨架式节奏序列。B 面迎来爆发，吉他被重塑为带有粗糙反馈共振和分裂式 riff 的声响武器，Guthrie 从轻柔的图案式鼓点骤然切换至爆炸性的爵士自由即兴，两人在呼吸间默契配合。专辑在柏林 Morphine Raum 演出现场录制，经一年后混音完成，封面设计亦被乐评单独提名。整张作品展现了长期合作者之间无需语言沟通的本能式互动，从极简悬置逐步推向高密度能量释放，最终收束于木管般的鸟鸣式泛音。

items.body: Improvisation, especially of the largely unplanned and entirely freeform variety, can be a bit hit-and-miss, particularly when it becomes apparent that the performers aren’t singing (or playing) from the same hymn sheet. Nevertheless, when collective interactions click into place—as on this seven-track mini-album by Alexander Varty on guitar & electronics, Andres Kahre on percussion and electric cello, and violin virtuoso Jack M Campbell—the results can be truly striking and illuminating. No Room For Error came about through a serendipitous encounter between Campbell and longtime collaborators Varty and Kahre on Gabriola Island (which lies in the Strait of Georgia in British Columbia), where Varty and Kahre reside. Campbell visited the island last summer on an artist’s residency funded by the Tommy Flowers Foundation to record his first solo album, Sounding Bombe: Enigma Project. The talented violinist soon teamed up with the two musicians, with sound engineer Jordan Koop taking care of mixing and mastering, and No Room For Error was born. One becomes immediately aware of a sense of place on any island, and one of the album’s strengths is the way it conjures a particular environment, climate and atmosphere. This is never presented in a programmatic way, however, but rather sensed through the music—leaving what’s heard open to the listener’s own interpretations. For example, the uneasy, unsettling ambience evoked in the three Haar-entitled tracks relates to the Scots word for a chilly, foggy easterly wind. However, low rumbling guitars, nervously shuttling strings, glitchy sound effects, and sudden jump cuts in Haar I hint at something more sinister. Think Helmut Lachenmann trapped in a Saw movie. Haar III almost made me jump out of my skin. No room for terror would have perhaps been a more appropriate title. Meanwhile, the opening of Smir (another Scots word, this time meaning ‘fine rain’) projects a lament-like quality, eventually building to a keening Ur Schrei of powerful proportions. Not all the tracks are dark and disturbing. As its title suggests, Nightswimming is surrounded by floating, suspended lines and shimmering timbres, its subtly immersive impact aided by Varty’s use of Trope software (developed by Brian Eno and Peter Chilvers). Meanwhile, Cosmophony feels like entering inside a futuristic spaceship’s generator and experiencing its pulsing hum. No Room For Error clearly benefits from Varty and Kahre’s intuitive understanding of each other’s aims—and how best to achieve them—shaped over time through a shared Alt Jazz aesthetic and projects involving the Gabriola Microsynth Orchestra (GMO). Equally impressive is the effortless way in which Campbell fits into the ensemble’s creative dynamics, his remarkable agility tempered by an innate musicality whose instincts tell him when, or when not, to play. This special synergy is heard especially in Haar II, throughout which Campbell shines, and in the brilliant Rumbledethumps, where each member of the trio is presented in turn—tremolando-like sweeps on violin and resonant percussive patterns by Kahre, followed by gritty Robert Fripp-meets-Derek Bailey punctuations on Varty’s processed guitar. No wonder Rumbledethumps has already gained traction amongst radio stations, including BBC Radio 3’s Late Junction. It’s almost the experimental music equivalent to a Taylor Swift song. What’s more, the album’s tracks never outstay their welcome, with only Nightswimming and Smir exceeding the five-minute mark. Whether intended or not, No Room For Error hints at the title of Hank Mobley’s seminal 1963 album No Room for Squares, which featured—in addition to the trailblazing saxophonist—a veritable who’s who of jazz luminaries, such as Lee Morgan, Andrew Hill, Herbie Hancock and Philly Joe Jones. No Room For Error may not sound like Mobley’s hard bop masterpiece, but its bold, innovative improvisatory approach and boundless creativity draw on its spirit. Experimental music du jour, and endlessly creative at that. The post No Room For Error (Redshift Records) appeared first on Sequenza21.
items._cn_summary: 这张七轨迷你专辑源于一次偶然的相遇：小提琴家Jack M Campbell在加拿大不列颠哥伦比亚省加布里奥拉岛艺术家驻留期间，与长期合作的吉他兼电子乐演奏者Alexander Varty以及打击乐兼电大提琴手Andres Kahre汇合，由此诞生了充满环境氛围的即兴合作。三人的自由即兴以苏格兰语词汇命名，如Haar（阴冷东风）和Smir（细雨），将地名、气候与感官体验转化为声响。Varty运用Brian Eno与Peter Chilvers开发的Trope软件生成漂浮声线，Kahre的低沉吉他轰鸣与神经质的弦乐穿梭交织，Campbell则以惊人的敏捷性融入三重奏的动力结构。专辑虽非程序化地描绘场景，却让人强烈感知到岛屿特有的环境氛围，时而阴暗不安、时而沉浸宁静。

items.body:
Over the course of the last decade, the group أحمد [Ahmed] has carved out a distinctive approach to the jazz canon through their tireless exploration of the music of Ahmed Abdul-Malik. Mining Abdul-Malik’s compositions and his incorporation of non-Western microtonality into the jazz vocabulary, pianist Pat Thomas, alto saxophone player Seymour Wright, bassist Joel Grip, and drummer Antonin Gerbal have done more than reinterpretation. They have used the music as a foundation for both immersion and subversion of the way that the standard jazz quartet functions within post-bop structures. For last year’s Sama'a (Audition), they went into the studio for an expansive refraction of Abdul-Malik’s Jazz Sahara. During that same session, the four took a slight detour to record Play Monk, a dive into deconstructions of six pieces by Thelonious Monk, all but one of which he recorded in the late 1950s when Abdul-Malik was part of his group. أحمد [Ahmed] has incorporated Monk tunes into their live sets but this is the first time they have focused on his tunes on a recording.

While Thomas, Wright, Grip, and Gerbal have not altered their strategies in the switch of source material, there is one significant shift in the way one listens to this music. A quick search returns no other versions of Abdul-Malik’s pieces other than those recorded by the composer or أحمد [Ahmed] whereas Monk’s “Epistrophy” or “’Round Midnight” have hundreds. Even a less well-known piece like “Oska T” has dozens. Because the pieces covered are so well known, their teasing apart and restructuring of the underlying thematic kernels are more readily evident. Over two CDs, the quartet digs in, with improvisations that range between 20 and 30 minutes with the exception of a seven-minute extrapolation of “Epistrophy.” These extended explorations allow the group to excavate the forms with a focused patience, zeroing in on and elucidating microscopic details, extricating them into the fundamental elements of penetrating improvisations.

The first phrases of the opening “Bye-ya / Epistrophy” provide a glimpse of what is to come. Bass and piano circle around the theme and Gerbal’s lithe drumming circles up to drive momentum. Wright’s stabbing alto picks apart the melody and the four launch off on a circuitous inquiry, dismantling Monk’s tune into its constituent fragments and then reassembling them with constructivist abstraction. Each of the four seize on elements of the underlying piece, playing them off of each other with unwavering resolve, an approach the group continues to advance in their sweeping live sets. There is an insistent intensity as Wright’s notes pick and prod at Thomas’ skewed clusters, Grip’s free walking lines, and Gerbal’s churning free rhythms. Shards of “Epistrophy” are introduced into the mix by Grip and Thomas, slowly accruing with multifaceted erudition.

The group continues to subvert expectations with “Friday the Thirteenth” as Thomas insistently repeats the first phrase of the tune against Grip’s growling arco inversions. Wright’s keypad pops and Gerbal’s open percussion build momentum and Wright unleashes spattered honks that open into a collective four-part splintering of the theme, picking it apart and recasting it with angular exactitude, building density and intensity over the course of the sweeping 26-minute improvisation. “’Round Midnight” gets a relatively straightforward introduction with Wright intoning the theme over sinuous bass and cymbal splashes. Thomas’ spare chords enter as the quartet dynamically transposes the constituent parts of the piece with imperturbable resolution resolving with the riveting cycling hushed snare abrasions that brings the piece to a close.

A seven-minute scorching, stuttering run through “Epistrophy” serves as an interlude to an abstracted, cascading reading of “Evidence” which takes Monk’s stop-start theme and explodes it with relentless, spiraled piano phrases and the hurtling momentum of bass and drums driving Wright’s coruscating alto which prods and jabs with spiky dexterity. The 30-minute improvisation is an engulfing exemplification of unflagging invention. Monk’s “Oska T.,” structured around an obsessively cyclical riff, is a fitting conclusion to the release. The quartet slows things down to a free shuffle with bass and alto arcing over the mutable pulse of piano and drums. The four players adroitly weave their lines in and out of the collective undercurrent with indefatigable ingenuity. While others have dedicated themselves to the reinterpretation of the music of Thelonious Monk, أحمد [Ahmed]’s Play Monk is distinctive in its mastery, fully absorbing his music into the collective rigor and artistry of this singular ensemble.

items._cn_summary: 这支伦敦即兴组合以爵士先驱阿卜杜勒-马利克为研究线索，将他与Thelonious Monk合作时期的六首作品作为拆解对象。钢琴Pat Thomas、高音萨克斯Seymour Wright、贝斯Joel Grip与鼓Antonin Gerbal四人延续他们对标准爵士四重奏结构的颠覆策略，将Monk的旋律骨架肢解为碎片，再以建构主义的抽象手法重新拼贴。曲目以二十分钟至半小时的长时间即兴展开为主，七分钟的《Epistrophy》例外。演奏过程强调微观细节的发掘与渐进式重组，四人各自分离主题元素，以固执的专注力相互碰撞。Thomas的偏斜音簇与Wright的刺入式高音线条持续角力，Grip的自由行走低音线与Gerbal的翻搅节奏提供底层张力，旋律残片在即兴推进中缓慢累积。这套双CD录音是组合首张以Monk曲目为核心的正式唱片，将熟稔旋律的陌生化处理推向纵深。

items.body: Last year we were introduced to the Ibiza-based NGO MusicForTheSea through Coco Francavilla’s liquid re-oceaning. This year the imprint’s second release was also unveiled on United Nations World Oceans Day, and celebrates the ocean while drawing essential attention to conservation efforts. Tidal Shifts – Reimagine, an outgrowth of an event in Nice, is a collaborative effort among field recordists, composers, and visual artists, incorporating copious underwater recordings from the Strait of Gibraltar captured by the Institute of Marine Research of the University of Cádiz. These recordings lie at the heart of the release, calling one’s ears ever back to the sounds of the sea. IDRA eases us gently into the ocean, beginning at the shore; the waves lap beside twinkling electronics and placid keys. Considering how many ambient tracks from Ibiza have showcased the sound of waves, it’s amazing that so few are this intentional; instead of mere background or sound effect, they are the music’s reason to exist. The soundings of Oora introduce the human element, studying the health of the ecosystem; the waves are louder, as is the rolling of the hull. This is the sound of research rather than intrusion, evidence of scientists hard at work. The “Tides at Bay of Fundy” are the world’s highest, yielding real-time evidence of glacial melt and climate change. As the music grows more active, one can imagine the tide rising, quicker and higher than expected, a parable for the planet’s possible fate. At the very end, there is only the sound of water, along with the sounding instrument; the music has abruptly recessed. Whalesong launchhes Vito Gatto‘s “Introimmersion,” wrapping the listener in a watery blanket. Cascades of keys pass by like schools of fish. Brass enters in the second minute, along with the crackle of what may be brine shrimp. The implication is of something dark and enormous; the question is, benign or threatening? Is this simply the shadow of a passing whale, or the longer shadow cast by the Great Pacific Garbage Patch? The closing “Indigo Reverie” is a collaboration between Kazuya Nagaya and Coco Francavilla, the former fresh from the release of Lumina. During this contemplative piece, one may indeed become lost in one’s thoughts, dreaming of the ocean and weekends by the sea. But to only do so is to miss the point. 15% of the world’s population lives by a coastline, while three times that number visit every summer. The coastline – as well as the health of the sea – is endangered, as are the lives of those who live in and around it. Tidal Shifts may sound comforting, but its intent is to unsettle, or at the very least to motivate. The beauty of “Indigo Reverie” is that it grows like a coral reef; but the music seems always fragile, a reminder that without care, even the most durable facets of life can disintegrate. (Richard Allen)
items._genre: ambient / field recording / contemporary classical / electronic
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由非营利组织MusicForTheSea发行，结合田野录音、电子音景与当代古典作曲，以联合国世界海洋日为契机发布。核心素材来自直布罗陀海峡的水下录音，由加的斯大学海洋研究所实地采集，真实记录了海洋生态系统的声学环境。专辑中IDRA的作品从岸边场景引入，海浪声与柔和电子键盘交融；Oora通过更响的浪声与船体滚动声呈现科学考察的声音质感；后续曲目围绕鲸鱼鸣叫展开，铜管声部在第二分钟进入，带来庞大而暧昧的声场。最终曲与Coco Francavilla合作，旋律以珊瑚礁式有机生长为隐喻，表面的安逸之下暗藏对海岸线生态危机与气候变迁的警示。整体音乐舒适但不流于装饰，借声音之美引导听众关注海洋保护议题。

items.body: Review by kev rowland — 'Fractal Guitar 4' is the fourth instalment in the 'Fractal Guitar' series which Swiss composer and guitarist Stephan Thelen initiated in 2015, with the last chapter being released in 2022. This is not the only series he has been working on and along with separate projects this is his 13th release since the first, which in itself was his 12th solo album outside of his work with Sonar. On this he again has multiple guests, many of whom he has worked with before, with only Norwegian guitarist Eivind Aarset playing on every track alongside Thelen, with the others contributing here and there. These include American guitarist Jon Durant, Israeli drummer Yogev Gabay, Markus Reuter from Germany (touch guitar), Fabio Anile from Italy (electric piano), Stefan Huth from Germany (touch bass guitar), Giri Subramaniam from India (tabla) and Andi Pupato from Switzerland (percussion), so a truly international line-up.When I started listening to this the first person I thought of was Allan Holdsworth, and that stayed true through the whole album although at times I also thought of John McLaughlin. One thing I found fascinating in that of all those involved, including Thelen himself, the musician I listen to most is Markus Reuter in multiple projects, yet here he is playing a role as opposed to driving music in his own manner, so his distinctive style is somewhat subsumed into the whole. One of the things which is fascinating with this album are the time signatures and polyrhythms being used, where musicians can actually be placing different signatures against each other which should lead to chaos both in the studio and in the brain but somehow it works, and I have no logical explanation as to why.If Gabriel was a guitarist as opposed to a singer I could imagine some of his early 80's albums sounding something like this, while King Crimson fans will also discover plenty here to enjoy as this is hugely complex and complicated, a music theorist's wet dream, yet there is also a clarity which makes it enjoyable as opposed to a chore. I cannot say this is overly easy to listen to, and is not for everyone, but if you want to hike through the pass less travelled you will find much more beauty than those who stay on the highways.
items._cn_summary: 瑞士吉他手与作曲家 Stephan Thelen 的《Fractal Guitar》系列第四辑，邀请了来自挪威、以色列、德国、意大利、印度、瑞士等地的多位乐手参与录制，是一张真正意义上的国际化合作专辑。核心双吉他配置由 Thelen 本人与挪威吉他手 Eivind Aarset 贯穿始终，其余乐手按曲风需要点缀加入，涵盖电钢琴、触弦吉他、贝斯、印度塔布拉鼓及多种打击乐器。整张专辑在复杂的复合节拍与多重拍号叠加中展开，多组不同节拍交错碰撞，制造出理论上应导向混乱的声响，却在精密编排下达到出人意料的平衡。评论将其置于 Allan Holdsworth 与 John McLaughlin 之间的吉他传统谱系中，同时关联 Peter Gabriel 早期作品的氛围感与 King Crimson 式的结构复杂度。专辑以数学化的节奏构思为骨架，却保留了清晰的听感层次，技术性与可听性并存，适合偏好前卫实验路线、愿意深入复杂音乐结构的听众。

items.body: Texan artist Rona Rougeheart has been active as SINE for several years, releasing music on labels such as Re:Mission, Emergency Hearts, and Negative Gain Productions. With “La Mordre”, however, she takes a major step forward, marking her debut release on Metropolis Records. “La Mordre” is a captivating musical experience—one that stands out for both its originality and its consistently high quality. Rather than sounding like a derivative of better-known acts, SINE has developed a distinctive sonic identity all her own. Her music seamlessly blends elements of Minimal-Electro, Dark-Pop, Industrial, and even touches of Hip-Hop into a cohesive and compelling whole. The album is built around deep, resonant bass tones, slow and seductive rhythms, and Rougeheart’s semi-spoken, sensual vocal delivery. Together, these elements create an atmosphere that is both unsettling and intensely alluring, balancing darkness with an undeniable sense of intimacy. From beginning to end, “La Mordre” delivers one outstanding track after another. Its hypnotic grooves and provocative mood make it the perfect soundtrack for an underground fetish club or a late-night Industrial dancefloor. This is an album that dares to be different—and succeeds with remarkable confidence. (Rating:8½). SINE released “La Mordre” in May 2026, a ten-track album that gathers four earlier singles alongside six new recordings. Listen to “Succumb To Me”: Succumb To Me by SINE About SINE SINE is the solo project of Rona Rougeheart, a drummer, vocalist, producer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Austin, Texas. Rougeheart uses the term “Electronic Boom” to describe the project’s sound, which blends sub-bass, beats, and industrial elements with lyrics that incorporate sarcasm, humour, and social commentary. The project’s early releases appeared on Austin’s eMERGENCY heARTS label. SINE’s 2021 album “Desire, Denial and Paramania” was released on 7 October 2021 and featured collaborations with Curse Mackey, producer Sean Beavan (Nine Inch Nails, 3Teeth), and vocalist Chris Connelly (Pigface, Revolting Cocks). The album also included a Meat Beat Manifesto remix by Jack Dangers. In January 2022, SINE released a remix of “Attack” by Adrian Sherwood on eMERGENCY heARTS, and in August 2022 issued the EP “Mantis 2” on the same label. SINE signed to Metropolis Records ahead of the 2024 album “Luxuria”, released on 19 January 2024. That record was produced by Claus Larsen of Leæther Strip and included the single “From Beyond” featuring Leæther Strip. Over the course of her career, Rougeheart has collaborated with Adrian Sherwood, Meat Beat Manifesto, Clan of Xymox, Chris Connelly, Mark Pistel, Andee Blacksugar (KMFDM, Blondie), Xiu Xiu, and the late Mark Stewart of The Pop Group. “La Mordre,” her second Metropolis release, arrives roughly two years after “Luxuria” and marks a step into a longer, more expansive album format.

items.body:
Returning after a 13 year absence, Boards of Canada's vision of hell isn't exactly surprising, swapping out the magic hour guitars of 'The Campfire Headphase' and the tired Carpenter-isms of 'Tomorrow's Harvest' for jagged distortions, dialog snippets and uneasy religious symbolism.

It can't be easy for Mike Sandison and Marcus Eoin; as soon as they cracked the code with 'Music Has the Right to Children' in 1998, their home-brewed signature sound - tape-warped, reverb-soaked monosynths, stuttering dialog samples and thumping MPC-breaks - became a sort of meme, regurgitated by a wave of bedroom musicians so frequently that the original references became fully hollow. Those early records were great because they sounded so unique, marking a landscape littered with post-'Chiastic Slide' crunches and choppy AFX-ian amens with new channels of thought. Just go back to their shadowy 'Twoism', 'Hi Scores', or that Mask 500 cover of 'Midas Touch' -  there was nowt else like it. By the time we got to 'The Campfire Headphase', a comparatively sunny, guitar-led misstep that arrived a few years later and then 2013's 'Tomorrow's Harvest' -  it all felt like diminishing returns.

'Inferno''s mysterious VHS rollout also felt overly familiar - and if you're gonna tease, the payoff best be worth it. Sadly, first single 'Prophecy At 1420 MHz' was damp and old fashioned, lumpen with boxy '80s drums and awkward prog rock synths - the signs didn't look good. Heard as a whole though, 'Inferno' hangs together pretty well. The brothers do a good job of laying out a vision of hell that's intricately connected to their well-worn source material: the lost future that was promised to wide-eyed 1970s kids raised on color TV, welfare and action figures. Back then, religious cults and street cranks were screaming of damnation, convincing weakened minds that judgement was coming while the Vietnam War raged - real hell was on the doorstep all along. And it's hard not to hear Boards' blend of seemingly old-fashioned religious symbolism (the Hare Krishna chants, chopped-up divinity school lectures and guided meditations) as an indirect reference to the wars raging right now. Certainly, it's their darkest album in years; not the aesthetic darkness of 'Tomorrow's Harvest', either. 'Father and Son', with its eerie Abrahamic symbolism, feels like an American Gothic reflection of Leslie Nielsen's comparatively benign narrations on 'Geogaddi', while 'Memory Death' feels like Boards actively sending off their own patented brand of hauntology with the EKG blip to prove it.

Throughout the record, BoC appear to juxtapose a cultural concept of hell with their own aesthetic responses, balancing dystopian robot voices with squelchy acid gurgles on the excellent 'The Word Becomes Flesh' and Bobby Beausoleil-style chiming strings on 'Blood in the Labyrinth'.  'The Process', meanwhile, offers a late-stage vision of aviation hell, a 'Langoliers'-style horror cue that neatly precedes the saccharine vintage BoC hit of 'You Retreat in Time and Space'. Perhaps unsurprisingly, it's these beatless moments that really hold things together - maybe they should have just leaned into it and done a full length of those vignettes. Still, 'Inferno' has its moments.
items._cn_summary: Boards of Canada暌违十三年推出的新作，以锯齿状失真音效、宗教对白片段与不安的宗教象征取代了此前的吉他质感与卡朋特式配乐。专辑构建了一幅关于地狱的文化图景，与七十年代电视文化、宗教狂热和越战阴影相呼应，哈瑞奎师那唱诵、神学院讲座采样与冥想引导被编织进层层失真的合成器纹理中。《The Word Becomes Flesh》将反乌托邦机器人声与酸性合成器声响并置，《Blood in the Labyrinth》则以Beausoleil式的钟弦乐暗示恶魔学氛围。评论认为单曲《Prophecy At 1420 MHz》表现乏力，但整张专辑作为概念整体连贯而沉重，是乐队近年来最黑暗的作品，延续了Geogaddi以来对美国哥特式意象的探索。

items.body:
The second ever public performance by Nurse With Wound, captured on tape in 1984 and held in Steven Stapleton's archive across the four decades since, now available on a vinyl edition for the first time - every copy painted by hand, edition of 300.

You get the measure of this one with Steven Stapleton’s assertion that this was less a gig and more a “series of confrontations with audiences who often had no idea what they were watching.” which is basically everything we hope for watching pretty much anything.

It belongs to a moment when Stapleton, working alongside collaborators including David Tibet, Andrew McKenzie of The Hafler Trio, and a rotating cast of percussionists and string players, was carrying NWW briefly out of the studio. The performance moves through the territory NWW had been mapping across Homotopy to Marie and Nature Unveiled: long passages of pre-recorded tape collage assembled by Stapleton and McKenzie, ridden over by live electronics, voice, percussion, and a surreal theatrical instinct.

or as the band call it, “a collective groping”

aye.

items._cn_summary: 1984年Nurse With Wound第二次公开演出的录音，四十年来首次以黑胶形式发行，每张手工绘制，限量300份。演出由Steven Stapleton与David Tibet、Andrew McKenzie（Hafler Trio）以及多位打击乐与弦乐演奏者共同完成，介于音乐会与一系列与观众的"对峙"之间。整场演出横跨预录磁带拼贴、现场电子、人声、打击乐与超现实剧场化的即兴，延续了《Homotopy to Marie》与《Nature Unveiled》时期的声音探索路线。乐评以简短的引述与乐队自嘲的"集体摸索"来勾勒这场演出的气质，强调其作为罕见档案文献的历史价值。整体文字精炼，信息密度适中，适合对工业实验与磁带文化感兴趣的听众。

items.body:
One half of Rezzett, Jackson ‘Tapes’ Bailey reels off a lush new age ambient / environmental soundtrack primed for deep immersion, originally intended for his partner’s food sculpture exhibition at Gianni Manhattan Gallery, now thankfully shared with the rest of us via Good Morning Tapes.

No dub or dungeon synfs here: instead, just under an hour of spirit-purifying, Kankyō Ongaku x olfactory synaesthesia, using a palette of vaporous electronics to suggest rich aromas, tastes, and fleeting tongue-tip sensations. The palette is minimal and evocative, gliding from exquisite, gossamer-soft FM synths, to a more reverential mode, glazed in sacred motifs.

For sound-bathing dreamers and anyone into Hiroshi Yoshimura’s OG environmental templates - this one’s a doozie.
items._genre: ambient / new age / environmental / sound sculpture
items._cn_summary: J Bailey（Rezzett二人组之一）以个人项目Tapes名义发布的原声带作品，最初为其伴侣在Gianni Manhattan Gallery举办的食物雕塑展览而创作。整张专辑时长不到一小时，以环境音乐和新世纪氛围为核心，刻意回避dub或地下club节拍，转向沉思冥想式的声景构建。制作中运用了飘渺的电子音色和FM合成器，呈现出极简而唤起感官的质感，借鉴了Hiroshi Yoshimura开创的环境音乐传统。乐评特别提及嗅觉联觉的听觉化处理——声音被用来暗示气味、味道与舌尖瞬间的感受，使听觉体验具有多感官的仪式感。由独立小厂牌Good Morning Tapes发行，具有明显的地下实验场景属性，适合深度沉浸式聆听与声浴场景。

items.body:
A decade since debuting as Ndagga Rhythm Force, Mark Ernestus’ incredible band draw on 100’s of hours studio and live practice for a staggering new suite of Senegalese x Berlin-styled mbalax steppers that prove, where needed, why they’re one of the best to do it right now. Absolutely exemplary, transcendent music for those that know.

Back at the start of the 2010s dub techno pioneer Mark Ernestus was spending a lot of time in Senegal, immersing in styles and patterns that historically underlined the reggae and dub musics he would heavily reference in his pivotal records made as Maurizio/Basic Channel/Rhythm & Sound, as co-produced with Moritz Von Oswald during the ‘90s and into the ’00s. 

In the process of researching and getting down to the roots of his passions, Ernestus encountered some of Senegal’s top tier musicians and recorded the Jeri-Jeri ensemble, revolving vocalist Mbene Diatta Seck and sabar drummer Bada Seck, and generating in 2013 the ‘800% Ndagga’ CD and its ’Ndagga Versions’ sibling, which better showcased Ernestus’ famed dub tekkerz inseparably woven into Senegalese music and the roots of myriad Afro-diasporic sounds.

That unit would morph into Ndagga Rhythm Force, producing an LP and trio of 12”s in 2015-2016 that set them on course to become one of the most impressive African bands on the contemporary gig circuit, throwing down live sets known to effortlessly go over 2 hours and propel so many legs and minds to new shapes and feels - trust they slay every time and should be top of all must-see lists.

With ‘Khadim’ Ndagga ditch their guitars and recalibrate a more lissom trio of voice and acoustic instruments bound with Ernestus’ Prophet 5 synth - the same model he’s relied upon since the Basic Channel days - on four extended songs that allow more light, space and emotion into a signature, rolling sound, centre-staging Mbene Seck’s husky diva croon over Bada Seck and Serigne Mamoune Seck’s dual, polymetric percussion, and judiciously juggled with Ernestus’ anti-gravity basses and plangent dub chord syncopation. 

In traditionally open-ended frameworks the quartet take all the time needed to stretch out and wrap heads into the tapestries of their storytelling grooves. A newfound atmospheric pressure and presence emerges in procession from the location recordings that fringe ‘Lamp Fall’ and its ode to a local mosque, reverberating in acres of implied space set by the ricocheting sabar drums and near-infrasonic subs, thru to the devotional depths of ’Nimzat’, rippling with thunderous chords and doleful ache. 

At its core are the LP’s most impressive parts; ‘Dieuw Bakhul’ uncoils a spellbinding Wolof tale of treachery to the rafters amid tempestuous chords that writhe stereo-wide with red-lining bite whilst drums knot sinuous, serpentine, to be resolved in the breathtaking 13’ steppers’ flight of ‘Khadim’, which lyrically hails Islam’s role in guiding Senegal to postcolonial times, spiritually meditates on bluest minor key riffs, and physically elevates bodies with aerodynamic finesse and hypnotic chronics kin to the best reggae and its offshoots. 

Deadly, soul and hoof gripping tunes. Do not miss!
items._genre: mbalax / dub techno / afro-diasporic fusion / experimental electronic
items._cn_summary: Ndagga Rhythm Force由dub techno先驱Mark Ernestus与塞内加尔音乐家共同打造，延续Basic Channel与Rhythm & Sound时期的dub美学底色，将塞内加尔传统mbalax节奏与柏林电子制作深度交织。专辑舍弃吉他编制，以人声、sabar鼓与Prophet 5合成器为核心，构建四首长篇作品。人声低沉沙哑，鼓组呈现复调多变的复合节奏，Ernestus的低频与dub和弦切分游离于传统泛音空间之外。'Lamp Fall'致敬清真寺的录音营造出深层环境氛围，'Khadim'以十三分钟展开伊斯兰引导塞内加尔走向后殖民时代的叙事，从低音小调riff中铺展冥想性张力。整体将非洲传统节奏体系、电子dub处理与仪式感场景融为一体，时间结构开放延伸，录音层次兼具现场呼吸与精密电子细节。

items.body:
Following Kuboraum's eccentric 2024 first volume, the Berlin-based eyewear brand and occasional label returns with another broad-minded statement of intent featuring some of the contemporary avant-garde's most visible figures, including Low Jack, bela, Richie Culver, Rainy Miller, EROS, Lucrecia Dalt, Lee Gamble, Ziúr and Significant Other.

The set opens on a wheezing, spitting and growling loosie from bela, whose sorely overlooked 'Korean Love Sonnets' full-length is still fueling our nightmares. From there, we stay locked into the outerzone with Kuboraum vet Cosimo Damiano, an Italian techno mainstay who's veered off path in recent years, hitting SUPERPANG with his modular experiment 'Multi-Species' and helming that killer Salò record from 2023. On 'Copper Disk' he conducts an unsettling ritual, shifting voices until only ghostly outlines remain and setting the stage for similarly strong voice experiments from Marina Herlop and the unstoppable Lord Spikeheart.

Prolific French producer Low Jack shifts the mood when he invites Le Diouck to help out on the grimy, groove-fwd 'TLC' and the motion is oddly maintained by Romain Azzaro's trap-gamelan hybrid 'Fusion' and Richie Culver's rainy 'C-SIDE', that sounds as if it could have slipped off his Fixed Abode debut 'I TRUST PAIN'. What keeps us gripped here though is that while 'Kuboraum Sound Residency Vol. 2' keeps reinventing itself, it carries a similar energy throughout, an air of glam, oily darkness that links Significant Other's grinding 'Lust On Your Shoulders' with EROS's menacing 'Burnt Crossing' and Emiliano Maggi's tape dubbed lullaby 'Fury'. Even a long "refurbished" version of Ziúr's 'Home' LP title track featuring cellist Martina Bertoni and Subtext's Sara Persico sounds as if it's been repainted in Kuboraum's distinct color scheme: darkened significantly, but just so the edges stand out more than ever before.
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑是柏林眼镜品牌Kuboraum旗下的第二期声音驻地计划，汇聚了Low Jack、Lucrecia Dalt、Lee Gamble、Ziúr等多位当代前卫音乐人。整张专辑贯穿一种油润的黑暗气质与诡异仪式感，从bela粗粝的人声拼贴开场，经过Cosimo Damiano模块化实验的幽灵化人声处理，再到Marina Herlop与Lord Spikeheart的声音实验，后续由Low Jack引入grime化律动，Romain Azzaro的trap与gamelan杂交、Richie Culver的阴沉氛围依次铺开。Ziúr的曲目被大提琴手Martina Bertoni重新编排后暗化处理，呈现更强的边缘感。全辑在多变形态中维持统一的暗黑光泽，展现出当代实验场景中跨艺术家策划合辑的连贯美学。

items.body:
alias Junior Rain are the duo of sound poet Francesco Cavaliere and sound artist Matteo Martino, minting Turin’s Isotopes Records with a tape of exquisitely heatsick wooze tipped FFO Spencer Clark, Jan Jelinek, Lieven Martens, NWAQ, Actress, Rezzet...

‘Capello di Cristallo’ could hardly be a more fitting soundtrack to the head-melting heatwave right now. For just shy of 30 mins, Cavaliere dials down his signature sound poetry to instrumental form, matched by Matteo Martino’s ear for textural, world-building detail, as previously revealed on his tape for ace DIY label Canti Magnetici. Across 11 works, the duo transcend the sum of their influences; whiffs of rearview vaporwave and new age ambient entwine around impulses from lo-fi Midwestern house, and its Euro offshoots, in a treacle-thick air oozing with ferric wow & flutter that sounds custom-made for high heat.

Subtly distinguished from Cavaliere’s decades of work by its slow burning rhythms, the album sways to its own dreamy pace thru pieces that melt into one another. The silvery chord bursts and busted drums of ‘in discesa’ feel like a knackered Sun Ra, and ‘espansione’ incurs Raul Lovisoni & Francesco Messina’s Cramps touchstone, hinting at a spiritual ambient jazz freeness that also colours their titular vacillation of lo-fi house, and the Rezzett-esque romance in ‘junior rain’ or ‘ragnelata magica’. 

Consider it a compliment to the artists that if you reach the end of the spool in an eyes-half-closed, bezonked state, their work here is done.
items._genre: experimental electronic / ambient / lo-fi house / sound poetry
items._cn_summary: 这是意大利都灵二人组 alias Junior Rain 在 Isotopes Records 厂牌发行的磁带专辑。声音诗人 Francesco Cavaliere 此次将人声剥离，专注于器乐层面的探索，与声音艺术家 Matteo Martino 的质地感音色设计相结合。十首作品相互渗透，以缓慢燃烧的节奏串联，散发出朦胧黏稠的氛围。银色和弦与破损鼓机交织，尾波蒸汽波、新世纪氛围与低保真中西部浩室在欧洲变体的框架中彼此缠绕。整体作品展现出对衰败质感与磁带失真的偏好，磁带的嘶嘶声与信号波动被保留下来，营造出夏日高温中融化流汗的听觉体验。厂牌定位 DIY 地下路线，融合爵士与电子的元素使其在风格光谱上具有较强跨界性。

items.body:
A parody of Brian Eno's 'Music for Airports' recorded at the heart of a banana plantation in Tenerife, Lagoss's 'Música para Plátanos' (music for bananas) is anything but background music, fixing up its ratcheting polyrhythms and "Latin-infused electronics" with flimsy exotica and oddball environmental recordings.

The music of 'Música para Plátanos' isn't just about the plantation, it attempts to live, breathe and exist just like the bananas themselves, reacting to each element whether it's the temperature or the nourishment. And the tracks came together over weekly improvised sessions recorded over the space of five years, where the trio of Gonçalo F. Cardoso, Mladen Kurajica and Daniel Baez tapped into their groove, fusing samples and tape loops with shifting percussive forms, instrumental outbursts and radio interference. If you heard 2024's 'Plátano Tapes', you'll have a good idea where the source of this record came from, but that collage has been worked into, shaved down, shaped and refined since then, distilled as a "greatest rotten hits" according to the press release, for an album that's meant to be distinct from their ongoing 'Imaginary Island Music' series.

It's good stuff, too, more engaging than you'd expect from a collection of jams, but then Lagoss are a force to be reckoned with. There's horizontal exotica - the organ-led 'Mundo Sour' and the skittering 'Plata no Police' - and plenty of oily ambient biz (just check 'Milliones de Gallinas'), but Lagoss are best when they're in a percussive groove. On 'Mosca Blanca / Horcón Girl', they muddle field recordings with low-slung bassy grooves and circuitous island rhythms, and 'Plátano Saki' is Tenerife in dub, a banana-themed, sun-bleached anthem that's seasoned with tape echo, reverb and manic Lee "Scratch" Perry-esque oscillations.
items._genre: experimental / electronic / exotica / world fusion / dub
items._cn_summary: 这是Lagoss乐队在特内里费香蕉种植园中心录制的一张专辑，戏仿Brian Eno的《Music for Airports》，将拉丁电子、异域元素与环境录音熔于一炉。三位音乐人历时五年进行每周即兴录音，将采样、磁带循环、打击乐形态与电台干扰拼接融合，使音乐试图模拟香蕉本身的生命状态，回应温度与养分的变化。相比此前更为粗糙的拼贴作品《Plátano Tapes》，这张专辑经过精炼与重塑，被乐评描述为一次成熟的蒸馏。专辑横跨慵懒的管风琴异域曲、油腻的氛围段落以及深沉律动的打击乐篇章，部分曲目带有dub质感与Lee "Scratch" Perry式的迷幻回声，整体呈现出热带即兴与电子实验交织的独特声响。

items.body:
Drawing on his experiences in Ghana, Niamké Désiré approaches his third record with a different energy, infusing his productions with noise and chaos to offset the fragile beauty of his work with violinist ASIA. RIYL Kevin Martin, Tim Hecker, Shapednoise or Ben Frost.

Describing his recent trip to Ghana as "an overwhelming, magnificent organization of noise," Désiré returned to Paris determined to shake up his methodology. He's already proven himself on albums like 2021's 'Simulacrum', 2023's 'Rhizomes' and last year's 'Ego Death' collaboration with Resina to be a prodigious sound designer and deep thinker, but he realised that it was stepping outside of his head that was needed. So, thinking about the journey rather than the destination, Désiré began to work on music with violinist ASIA for a Parisian commission that was more assertively personal, considering the actual feeling of "diasporic in-betweenness" he experienced as he moved between Paris and Ghana, rather than speculating on philosophy. The result was '100 Soleils', a lengthy composition that Désiré splits into four pieces on 'The Sun Turned Black', using it as a blueprint for the feel of the entire record. 

Threaded through with ASIA's delicate string work, Désiré's newfound confidence in noise evolves over the course of almost half an hour, giving Désiré's competent sound design the fangs it needed. There's natural chaos to the soundscape he creates on '100 Suns, Pt. II', animalistic screeches that complement his digitally-shaped elements, and we begin to sense an interplay between very different worlds. Désiré creates the same friction between the electronic and acoustic instrumentation, building vast artificial melodic structures on the towering '100 Suns, Pt. III' and resolving them on the fourth chapter with ASIA's sweeping strings. Breaking up the piece, 'The Children of Noise' establishes dissonance and the title track acts as a brief, gratifying conclusion, finding harmony between the desiccated, buzzing noise and Désiré's richly textured harmonic clouds.
items._genre: experimental electronic / drone / noise / contemporary composition
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是尼维斯·德西雷的第三张全长作品，他以加纳旅行为灵感，将个人在巴黎与加纳之间辗转所感受到的离散经验转化为声音创作。核心曲目《100 Soleils》原本为巴黎委约而作，与小提琴家ASIA合作完成，全长近半小时，被拆分为四个乐章贯穿整张唱片。德西雷作为声音设计师的功底扎实，此前的《Simulacrum》《Rhizomes》等作品已建立口碑，而本作的转变在于他将外部世界的混沌引入创作。有机的小提琴弦乐在电子噪音与数字塑形声响之间穿梭，形成人工旋律结构与原声乐器之间的张力。专辑探讨离散身份的夹层体验，用噪音与颤栗音色编织出兼具破坏力与脆弱感的音景。

Embarking on the Caretaker’s final journey with the familiar vernacular of abraded shellac 78s and their ghostly waltzes to emulate the entropic effect of a mind becoming detached from everyone else’s sense of reality and... more
items.body:
The first three albums in the 'Everywhere At The End Of Time' series in one set - two and a half hours long, each album reveals new points of progression, loss and disintegration, falling further and further towards the abyss of complete memory loss and nothingness...

Embarking on the Caretaker’s final journey with the familiar vernacular of abraded shellac 78s and their ghostly waltzes to emulate the entropic effect of a mind becoming detached from everyone else’s sense of reality and coming to terms with their own, altered, and ever more elusive sense of ontology. The series aims to enlighten our understanding of dementia by breaking it down into a series of stages that provide a haunting guide to its progression, deterioration and disintegration and the way that people experience it according to a range of impending factors.

In other words, Everywhere At The End of Time probes some of the most important questions about modern music’s place in a world that’s increasingly haunted or even choked by the tightening noose of feedback loops of influence; perceptibly questioning the value of old memories as opposed to the creation of new ones, and, likewise the fidelity of those musical memories which remain, and whether we can properly recollect them from the mire of our faulty memory banks without the luxury of choice.
items._cn_summary: 这是Leyland Kirby「管家」计划的代表作，以磨损的78转虫胶唱片和幽灵般华尔兹为素材，模拟痴呆症患者意识逐渐剥离现实的过程。整部作品分为六个阶段，黑胶套装收录前三阶段共两个半小时，每一阶段都呈现记忆衰退的不同层次——从熟悉旋律的缓慢变形，到旋律碎片化的迷失，直至完全陷入虚无。作品借助声学退化效果处理老录音，探讨记忆的不可靠性与时间对感知的侵蚀，同时触及老音乐在新语境中的存续问题。这种将音乐媒介本身的物理衰老作为隐喻的手法，使其成为对退化、失落与本体论消解的深层冥想。

items.body: Knowing what Foel built this record out of—a difficult mental health stretch, a fascination with landscapes that are beautiful and hostile in equal measure, a process built on chaos eventually resolving into order, Gwasgaru earns its title honestly. “Shaped randomness” Gwasgaru by Foel   Jack Smith-Keegin spent twenty years building toward this. The North Wales-based producer behind Foel started making music at sixteen, but didn’t release anything until 2025’s Ogof Melltydd single on WEPN, two decades of self-taught tool-building before he felt ready to put anything out into the world. A Welsh speaker raising two children with his wife in the mountains and coastlines of North Wales, his musical entry point traces back to hearing Boards of Canada‘s Geogaddi at fifteen, an album he describes as hitting him straight in the heart. That door opened onto Warp, Plaid, Aphex Twin, Venetian Snares, and eventually Autechre—Draft 7.30 specifically, which he says didn’t click at first but became an obsession once it did. Gwasgaru—Welsh for “scatter” or “disperse“—was built mostly in Bitwig using its modular grid, alongside a custom Node.js program with a CSound backend that Foel describes as more than vapourware but not yet fully composition-ready. His process leans heavily on repeatable randomness—generating outcomes he can hunt through and refine, rather than gravitating toward what he already knows. It’s a technical approach in service of something deeply personal: Foel made this album during what he describes as a genuinely difficult stretch with his mental health, and the record carries that weight throughout. The album’s opener is mature in its composition because i​t doesn’t set you up for anything you’d expect it to sound like. This is something deeper. The drums build into nothingness, kicks fading into the abyss of sound, layering as it continues toward the track’s end. “Rhewlif” has an interesting sound too, with its rhythm and melodic composition. At points it sounds and feels almost random, and it very well might be, nothing here sounds planned, nothing settles into a repetitive, catchy melodic pattern. That’s a deliberate choice rooted in how Foel works. Generative and randomized approaches to melody in IDM typically still operate within a defined scale or harmonic boundary, the notes are unpredictable in sequence but never unpredictable in pitch relationship, which means the result feels alive and unrepeating without ever sounding atonal or aimless. Foel‘s own description of “shaped randomness” fits exactly into that tradition. One thing already standing out in Foel‘s work is the production technique of introducing new elements midway through a long track’s build. Partway through this track, he uses very sharp filtering on the bass synth, almost like lasers cutting through the waveform—a technique close to what’s sometimes called ducking, where one sound is compressed and pushed down in response to another. In layman’s terms: imagine the bass and another element fighting for the same space, and a compressor automatically lowers the volume of one every time the other hits, so they never collide and mask each other. It’s commonly used to let a kick drum punch through a bassline in dance music, but Foel applies it more abstractly here, using it almost as a rhythmic device in its own right rather than just a mixing utility. That’s what’s happening in this track, and it genuinely gives the piece its personality as it continues, almost as if the track is disintegrating from the inside. Almost like little nothings threaded through reverb stabs and drums :: “Chwil” is another strange builder and by builder, this means Foel continues the theme of constructing anticipation across each track, whether through drums or melody, giving the listener’s ears a ride rather than a destination. Melody isn’t the focus here, which fits Foel‘s more experimental background showing through. “Dadmer” enters next and is genuinely a standout. The ducking concept reappears here, but this time the melodic note feels like it’s complementing the snare at the same moment, which creates an enjoyable experimental effect. Visually, it’s like the melody is a ping pong ball and the kick and snare are playing ping pong with it, batting it back and forth until it fades into nothing. “Ar goll” is full of dark drums and ambience that grows almost frantically in a space obsessed with reverb and compression. “Gwasgiad” functions as a part two of that idea, but cleaner in its approach, there’s a resemblance now to Autechre‘s Quaristice in its sound design sensibility, and the drum and snare programming here is genuinely excellent. The closer, “Gwasgaru,” is a dark IDM track where Foel plays the melody far back in the mix, almost like little nothings threaded through reverb stabs and drums. If there’s a theme running through this album that’s used well, it’s that ducking technique, deployed multiple times, clearly a recurring tool Foel reaches for strategically across these productions, and it’s exactly what makes them stand out as genuinely interesting to listen to. Knowing what Foel built this record out of—a difficult mental health stretch, a fascination with landscapes that are beautiful and hostile in equal measure, a process built on chaos eventually resolving into order, Gwasgaru earns its title honestly. By the closing track, that small melody really does sound like it’s floating away over the mountains, and you believe it. Art by: Ben Hendon Gwasgaru is available on Machine. [Bandcamp] Gwasgaru by FoelThe post Foel :: Gwasgaru (Machine) first appeared on Igloo Magazine.
items._cn_summary: Foel的首张专辑《Gwasgaru》在Bitwig的模块化网格与自研Node.js+CSound程序中完成，核心方法是"可重复的随机性"——生成大量素材后筛选打磨，而非依赖既有直觉。这一生成式流程继承自Boards of Canada、Autechre一脉的IDM传统，却带有强烈的个人印记：威尔士山海岸线的自然意象、二十年的自学沉淀、心理健康低谷期的情感重量。专辑拒绝重复性旋律模式，鼓组从零累积又消散于声音深渊，低音合成器在中段以锐利滤波切入，类激光切割波形的段落成为其标志性手法。整张作品在混沌与秩序之间寻找平衡，"散落"这一威尔士语专辑名既是技术描述也是情感出口。
