items.body:
This New World CD is by my count the fourth or fifth edition in half a century of a record that should never go out of print. Julius Hemphill released it on LP soon after its 1972 recording on his Mbari label. (Its name is writ large on the original cover; his own name did not appear. New World adds it to the facsimile cover.) He distributed it himself, and not many copies circulated. The album came out to a larger world with the 1977 version in Arista/Freedom’s new music series, with a new and striking cubistic photo-montage cover by Dennis Pohl, and liner notes by Robert Palmer which told us a bit about the West African Dogon people, and about Fort Worth–reared St. Louis–seasoned Hemphill. Curiously Palmer never IDs the backbones of Hemphill’s backbeat, cellist Abdul Wadud and ex-Paul Butterfield, ex-Art Ensemble of Chicago drummer Philip Wilson. (He did mention Julius’ right hand, trumpeter Baikida Carroll.) Advance word of a sort had come the previous year, with the release of Hemphill’s Arista/Freedom Coon Bid’ness, mostly recorded in 1975. It included “The Hard Blues” left over from the 1972 session, a tune which added Hamiet Bluiett’s bari to the core tet. A 2011 (pricey) limited edition CD miniaturizing the Pohl/Palmer package was produced by International Phonograph’s late Jonathan Horwich, who remastered the program from the original tapes, sensibly tacking on “The Hard Blues” as a bonus track. So does the New World version, which also sports new notes by Hemphill colleague/scholar/archivist Marty Ehrlich. The sound has been newly refurbished by Paul Zinman, cleaning up the raggedy/degraded tape ending of “Rites.” (I haven’t seen it, but there’s also a new Superior Viaduct LP edition of the original program/artwork, with notes by John Corbett.)

Wadud’s cello voice is prominent on Coon Bid’ness’ choogling “Skin 1” and “Skin 2,” but even with that album to whet a new Hemphill fan’s appetite, Abdul’s entrance at the top of Dogon’s 15-minute opening/title track was a stunner. First time I heard it, 49 years ago, I fell in love with the album before Julius had sounded a note: Wadud’s grinding one-bar bowed-dyads ostinato turned cello into a big Delta blues guitar. Wadud wasn’t the first jazz cello player by a long shot, though earlier ones mostly treated it like a baby bass. Other improvising cellists cropped up in the 1970s – Diedre Murray, David Eyges, Tristan Honsinger, Tom Cora, Ernst Reijseger ... – with many more soon to come, but nobody brought earthy sensibility and downhome funk to intonation and frictive bowing like Wadud. “Dogon”’s grinder riff nestled in the cracks in Philip Wilson’s sparse 11/16 drums and cymbal tattoo (a 4+4+3 he found tricky to master and held onto, tight, for most of it). And then come the horns, alto and trumpet melded in unison, and occasional blue minor harmony, phrasing like a single entity – the yoked horns of World Saxophone Quartet coming. (WSQ was already active when Arista/Freedom’s Dogon came out.) That melody is a series of bluesy aphoristic phrases that build on what’s already unfolded, then atomizes into a series of exclamatory single notes. The overall structure mirrors that odd-meter bar: the main melody’s sections are 19, 11 and 13 bars long.) In practice the melody seems capable of infinite development, while leaving space for cello and drums to speak through. (The cello part’s built-in variations may outline the harmony, arco or pizz.) And then comes Hemphill’s alto solo over vamping. Ornette’s North Texas holler is somewhere in the distance behind it, but Julius’s tone is dryer and harsher, his blues-infused intonation more sour and pitiless, his wildly scouring line informed by the written material: it’s all of a piece. He boils over and keeps boiling. (Baikida eases into his spot – won’t compete with that.) The blues gets dehydrated and reconstituted.

“Dogon A.D.” is all slow build; swifter “Rites” plunges right into the twisty melody; we’re in the thick of action from the opening seconds, fast but with no fixed tempo, its recurring hook (and opening) a couldn’t-be-simpler drop of a whole step. Thick is right: three-part harmony with cello as third horn, or sometimes as droning tambura. (If Ornette’s in there, it’s the roiling Crisis.) Baikida is especially effective darting behind Julius, blowing bugler’s commentary, reinforcing but never upstaging the boss’ alto. “Rites” is all coiled energy; when it flags, return to the head for a quick exit. For still more contrast, there’s the slowly unwinding “The Painter” for Hemphill’s bucolic sung-multiphonics flute (refreshingly un-Rahsaan-like), its melody both wide-ranging and sing-song catchy. Timing and articulation can be tricky – it’s not a line a part-time flutist writes for an easy layup. Wadud strums or picks rhythm; Wilson rustles; Carroll is as ever the loyal supporter, nimbly selfless, has chops to burn but keeps them in check. It’s the composer’s show, even without Hemphill’s name on the original cover.

And then “The Hard Blues” with its stompy riffy head, looking directly ahead to (and featuring half of) WSQ, but also – with its achingly-slow-to-quick tempos and dense-to-lean textures, suite-like variety and scored interludes – to Henry Threadgill’s 1980s Sextett. Whatever else he did, Julius Hemphill (like other members of St. Louis’s BAG co-op) brought convincing funk to new acoustic jazz, and reaffirmed the blues as eternal wellspring. Timeless tunes, an original group sound, liberatory cello – their appeal does not wear thin. Ehrlich’s notes describe in detail a private video of an earlier performance of the “Dogon A.D.” suite including a first unrecorded movement. The quartet was Hemphill, Carroll, Wilson and pre-Wadud pianist John Hicks, on vibes, playing what I’ve always thought of as the idiosyncratic ‘cello part.’ I imagine this performance as something from an alternate universe, one where Hemphill never performed at Oberlin College in 1970, and never met and jammed with the cellist known to classical audiences as Ronald DeVaughn, and that earthy blue arco scrape never got to shake us to the core.

Ideally Dogon A.D. and Coon Bid’ness should be reissued together, a definitive picture of Hemphill’s (and Wadud’s) music in early bloom. Rights to both are currently held by Germany’s DA Music. But both together are just too long to fit on a single CD. (With thanks to Marty Ehrlich for fielding various questions.)

items.body:
LOCAL（国内）
NEWS
ALM（コジマ録音）から新作２タイトル・リリース
八巻志帆『EVOKE』とマックス・デヴロー『レジスタンス』
2026年7月5日
編集部

ALM（コジマ録音）からユニークな新作２タイトルがリリースされる。バスクラリネット奏者八巻志帆の『EVOKE』とエレクトリック・ギター奏者マックス・デヴローの『レジスタンス』。

心のなかの音に、もういちど出会う

『EVOKE』（ALM3138) は八巻志帆の４作目のアルバム、八巻と中村奈央の２バスクラリネットによるフロントが、柳原由佳 (p) 、伊東佑希 (b)、則武諒 (ds) のピアノ・トリオと組むクインテット。18年にわたってバスクラリネットと向き合ってきた八巻が自身の音楽観をあらためて見つめ直した先に生まれたアルバムで、ジャズやクラシックなどのボーダーを超えてバスクラリネットを媒介として紡がれる音楽の美しさを、オリジナルやカヴァーを通して、きわめて率直な形で提示する。

試聴サイト；
https://kojimarokuon.com/products/alm-3138?_pos=2&_sid=3313df8c3&_ss=r

「抵抗」を原理としたプロセスと音楽

ミネアポリスを拠点とする作曲家・ギタリスト、マックス・デヴロー（1994–）は、映像・絵画・いけばなまで手がける分野横断的アーティストで、現代アメリカのアヴァンギャルド・シーンで独特の存在感を放つ。現代音楽、電子音響、サウンド・スタディーズ（音響文化論）の交点に位置するリリースは日本を含む各国レーベルから100を超え、坂本弘道、羽野昌二、吉田隆一といった日本の即興・前衛音楽アーティストとの協働も重ねている。本作《レジスタンス》は2026年作曲、デヴロー自演のギター独奏によってリアライゼーションされた音源。音楽のストーリー性ではなく発音方法・持続的注意・時間の物質性を強調する思弁的かつ透徹とした音響作品。不特定楽器またはアンサンブルのための図形記譜は、作品の個の強度と同一性を保ちながら、同時に分断を越えた連帯とヴァリエーションの可能性に開かれている。（本作の図形楽譜をブックレットに収載）

https://kojimarokuon.com/products/alm-149?_pos=1&_sid=82fc6fe8d&_ss=r
items._genre: avant-garde / free improvisation / contemporary classical / experimental
items._cn_summary: ALM厂牌同期发行两张新作。巴克拉管演奏家八卷志帆的第四张专辑《EVOKE》以双巴克拉管领奏搭配钢琴三重奏，跨越爵士与古典边界，以原創与翻奏作品呈现木管乐器的音色美感与率直表达。吉他演奏家马克斯·德夫罗的《レジスタンス》以2026年作曲的吉他独奏形式发行，强调发音方法、持续性注意与时间的物质性，附有图形乐谱，兼具思辨性与演奏开放性。德夫罗跨越影像、绘画与花道等领域，与多位日本即兴与前卫音乐家保持合作，作品定位处于现代音乐、电声音响与声音研究的交汇点。两张专辑均强调演奏者的个人艺术观与跨媒介表达。

items.body:
Part 1 of a 12" series featuring Beatrice M.’s 'Sinking', the rudely aerodynamic debut LP where Tectonic's franco-british hope flexes a signature balance of ruff & smooth, building on a solid reputation earned via 12”s with her label, Bait, plus Tempa and Darwin’s SPE:C.​

Dubstep is not necessarily an album genre: beyond scant examples from the likes of Burial, Shackleton, or 2562, 12”s and DJ sets serve the sound in best context. However, Beatrice M.’s grasp of subtle sensuality and propulsive traction patently ends itself well to the format on ’Sinking’, with rolling, stepping and skanking permutations that deftly dance in the space between dubstep, proper, and its close-related cousins - UKG, broken beat, dub techno - with a finely measured proprioception of space, weight and pressure. 

Along with 2562’s recently dispensed ‘Lost Dubs 2006-09’, ’Sinking’ is arguably the best thing on Tectonic in recent memory, with a sound that revels in more ambiguous club suss. It’s the type of release primed for cans/buds as much as big cones, proving she’s equally adept at sublime tension, as in the languid ‘Ever’, as propelling a dance in the Martyn-esque wriggler ‘Motion’, and offbeat hood of ‘Disco Corner’.
items._genre: dubstep / electronic / UK bass / broken beat / dub techno
items._cn_summary: 这是Beatrice M.在Tectonic厂牌发行的首张全长专辑，作为12寸单曲系列的延伸呈现。她以dubstep为核心骨架，巧妙游走于UKG、broken beat与dub techno等近亲风格之间，在律动、空间感与重量感之间拿捏出精妙的平衡。专辑并非典型的俱乐部工具，而是展现出多面性格：既有慵懒舒缓的暗流（如'Ever'），也有Martyn式的扭动推进（如'Motion'），以及offbeat律动的'Motion'式作品。整体制作注重细腻感官与张力铺陈，既适合耳机细品，也适配大型音响系统。评论将其与2562的近期作品并列为Tectonic近年最佳，凸显其在当代dubstep场景中对柔韧与粗粝并存质感的独特掌控。

items.body:
Rezzett come hungry for the club with a volley of thizzing ghetto-tech and breakbeat hardcore hot on the heels of their debut album

For the DJs, dancers, and anyone needing to extend the pleasures of their eponymous LP, ‘Boshly’ sees Lukid & Tapes’ razz out from a corkscrewing mutation of jungle tekno in the title tune, to thee most febrile takes on ’93 hardcore gnash in the delirious ‘Dots’ and the free-handed jungle of ‘Kermit’, with an appropriate come down in ‘Extra Redundant’, each treated to their patented, astringent tekkerz.
items._genre: jungle / hardcore breaks / ghetto-tech / experimental electronic
items._cn_summary: Rezzett 的第二张发行延续了首张专辑的俱乐部美学，将 jungle tekno、93 年 hardcore breakbeat 与 ghetto-tech 编织成一张面向 DJ 与舞池的舞曲拼贴。标题曲以螺旋式的 jungle tekno 突变开场，Dots 滑向九十年代初 hardcore 的狂躁音色，Kermit 则展开自由流动的 jungle 节拍，Extra Redundant 作为收束提供必要的喘息空间。制作上延续其标志性的尖锐音色处理手法，每首曲目都经过独特的声学塑形。Lukid 与 Tapes 两位成员以俱乐部需求为出发点，将旧时代英国 hardcore 与 jungle 语汇进行当代重构，既保留亚文化根源又注入实验性变异。整体定位介于复古回溯与地下实验之间，对电子音乐尤其是 jungle/hardcore 谱系感兴趣的听众具有较高参考价值。

items.body:
Produced by Neek and Jabu's Amos Childs (aka O$VMV$M), Manonmars' third album is syrupy suite of smoke-hazed recollections and free associated reflections set to decelerated, semi-rhythmic bumps, sluggish samples and cloudy drones. Sturdy biz FFO Ka, MIKE, King Vision Ultra or Coby Sey.

Manonmars' 2018 debut is one of those albums we still go back to periodically. It's that rare meeting of minds: a space for O$VMV$M to flex their production muscle and a scratchpad for London-based MC, painter and photographer Jack Martyn Richardson to sketch out his vision of England. And his experiences and impressions on 'Entertainment System' still feel chewable. "Goddess on my arm and both our phones got no service," he quips on 'Goddess'. "Acid is lysergic, psychedelic rock is Turkish." His rhymes aren't throwaway, they map out an underground that's very recognisable, shadowed by O$VMV$M's tuff, effective soundscapes - beats that reference trip-hop, ambient music, exotica and '70s movie soundtracks as much as they do US rap. On opener 'Flam3throw3r', Mars raps in double-time over shrill horns that blot out any trace of a beat; Neek and Childs sound as if they're relishing the negative space, adding chic sword swipes to a track that's got little else to do with the Wu Tang Clan. And even when a lumbering beat kicks in on 'Decathlon', flipping from downtempo to no-tempo in the final act, it sounds as if it's just there to assert O$VMV$M's commitment to slowness - Mars doesn't even seem to notice, rhyming casually but never losing his internal flow.

On 'Nasyua', his slurred expressions duck and weave around industrial whirrs and animalistic groans. "There was a time when I had flaws now I've adapted," he slurs. "I hit the zoot like Steve Zissou in 'The Life Aquatic' / then I dashed it, Christian Bale in a facemask on some Bat shit." Bristol mainstays Franco Franco and Dali de Saint Paul turn up to assist on 'Volcanic Shield', one of the album's most conventional bangers, led by O$VMV$M's skittering Surf Gang-like beats and morse code blips, and cold light's Birthmark lends his voice to 'Infinite', going bar for bar with Mars over Neek and Childs' soupy slackened funk. These moments are when 'Entertainment System' really shines, blaring out like an old tape on a busted in-car audio system. 'Firewater' takes the same approach, leaving Mars to do his best as snares are reformed into splashes alongside sultry stabs and sax from Brum-based sound artist Lorenzo Prati. "My bitch white, she can scuba dive and ice climb," he spits. "Put the drink down, I wasn't in my right mind." It's music that laughs through the tears - what could be more British than that?
items._genre: abstract hip-hop / experimental electronic / lo-fi / ambient rap
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由Neek与Amos Childs（合称O$VMV$M）担纲制作，是伦敦MC Jack Martyn Richardson的第三张作品，呈现一种减速、烟雾弥漫的声音美学。制作上混合了trip-hop、ambient、exotica与七十年代电影配乐的质感，鼓点常处于半节奏或无节奏状态，缓慢的采样与朦胧的drone铺底，留出大量负空间。Richardson的说唱风格松弛、双倍速自由流动，歌词记录英国地下场景的日常观察与文化碎片，引用从Bill Murray到Christian Bale的影视意象。客串阵容包括Bristol与Birmingham的艺术家，为部分曲目加入工业噪音、sax与funk元素。整体气质介于抽象嘻哈与实验电子之间，以松散的低保真制作承载叙事性的口语诗。

items.body:
Airbrushed, subtropical, new age ambient-jazz from Jesse Peterson’s Maui-based project, given its highest profile platform to date on Amsterdam’s Music From Memory, and warmly advised to admirers of his regular spars, Carlos Niño, Laraaji, Mia Doi Todd...

"Originally formed in New York in the late 2000s, Turn On The Sunlight has evolved into a fluid, location-spanning practice rooted in collaboration, intuition and process. Now based on Maui, Peterson’s work draws together a wide network of musicians and environments, with recordings taking shape across Los Angeles, Tokyo, London, San Miguel de Allende and Haʻikū.

Loosely situated within a framework of organic, ambient-leaning jazz, 'Iseo' unfolds as a series of open, exploratory pieces, with electronics sitting subtly beneath acoustic and environmental elements. Built from layered instrumentation including synthesizers, guitar, zither, flutes, voice and field recordings, Peterson moves between grounded, tactile detail and more expansive, immersive states. A sense of warmth and permeability runs throughout: organic percussion, environmental textures and drifting rhythmic elements lend the record a gently saturated humidity, reflecting Peterson’s base in Hawaii, where the presence of nature is felt as much as it is heard.

Underlying the project is a way of working rooted in gathering, listening and tending. Instruments, ensemble sessions, field recordings and everyday environments are approached with attentiveness, shaped through collecting, refining and allowing things to settle. Relationships, landscape and lived experience shape the sound, giving 'Iseo' a tactile, almost hand-made quality.

Rather than fixed arrangements, the album feels as if it has been organically and lovingly assembled through a process of listening and response, each element finding its place within a wider, evolving whole. This approach reaches a natural centre point in the 15-minute piece 'Medianoche En La Calle Aurora', which unfolds patiently, bending through shifting environments as motifs and textures emerge and dissolve with quiet continuity.

Peterson’s role as both instigator and facilitator is central to the project. Bringing together a diverse group of collaborators including Carlos Niño, Mia Doi Todd, Laraaji, Ko Ishikawa, Luis Pérez Ixoneztli and Miles Spilsbury, he creates space for individual voices to emerge within a shared language. The result is a music defined by openness and generosity.

'Iseo' takes its title from Peterson’s son’s middle name, a word that can be understood to mean ‘one-world life’. The piece itself takes the form of a gentle lullaby, its melody loosely shaped around the syllables of his name and sung to Peterson’s son by Luis Pérez Ixoneztli, a close collaborator whose presence across the record reflects a long-standing relationship that extends beyond the music itself.

Sleeve art and design by Michael Willis."
items._genre: ambient / new age / organic jazz / world fusion
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由Jesse Peterson在Maui创建的项目Iseo发行，是一张充满亚热带气息的有机氛围爵士作品。录制跨越洛杉矶、东京、伦敦、圣米格尔阿连德与海库等地，融合合成器、吉他、齐特琴、笛声、人声与田野录音等多层元素。整张专辑呈现出开放的探索性结构，电子元素轻柔地隐于原声乐器与环境声之下，带有湿润饱和的热带氛围。15分钟的《Medianoche En La Calle Aurora》是核心曲目，乐器与人声在不同环境中自由浮现又消散。合作者包括Carlos Niño、Laraaji、Mia Doi Todd等独立音乐人，协作模式强调倾听、回应与自然的集结过程。标题曲《Iseo》取自Peterson儿子中间名，由Luis Pérez Ixoneztli以摇篮曲形式演绎，旋律围绕名字音节展开。专辑由阿姆斯特丹小厂牌Music From Memory发行，整体概念强调跨地域协作与声音的开放性。

items.body:
Nkalipho Andile Mkhize aka Akiid blazes thru with 11 sharp sidespins on gqom, ama & Afrotech, inflected with Jersey club, trance, trap and techno - all demonstrating why he’s one of Durban’s rising stars.

‘Skeffu’ hustles some of the hottest strains of harder-edged club and street rave emerging from South Africa in the mid 2020s. The distinct sound speaks to Akiid’s peripatetic youth, moving between Durban townships where he picked up myriad local styles and patterns which fed into his rudely mutable and robustly disciplined sound. Call it gqom 2.0, hybrid Afrotech, or the Future Sound of Durban; whatever, it’s properly effective dance music certain to catch fire far beyond the source.

Fierce from front to back, ‘Skiffu’ is emblematic of the way SA artists absorb virulent sounds into their very particular dance vernacular. A youthful zeal for the thrills of contemporary Black Atlantic sounds - Jersey club, ATL trap, Chi & LDN drill - is factored by production techniques from megadome EDM, dub techno and even psytrance, to generate a ceaseless FWD traction in its pointed limb/limbic triggers. It’s all there in the breathless tension of ‘Chuck Norris’ and most impressive on the sound design staging of ‘MoonWalk Two’, where Jersey drill-type bass and an almost Burial-esque woodblock ushers detuned, mentasm-like licks to a heart-in-mouth breakdown.

As with any style, it’s possible to reach a point of saturation or exhaustion before the ears reach overfamiliarity and seek new thrills, and its maybe fair to say gqom hasn’t offered all that much that’s new in recent times (or at least that we’ve caught on to). But Akiid’s lust for fresh pressure, as heard on the angler canter of the title track, or his chimeric Jersey club x trance stabbed with isiZulu calls and scratch motifs in ‘Emotional Damage’, acutely remedy that issue with a thrilling, recombinant sense of club dramaturgy.

TIP!
items._cn_summary: 南非德班制作人Akiid的首张专辑《Skeffu》收录11首作品，以gqom与Afrotech为基底，融合Jersey club、trance、trap和techno等多种当代俱乐部音乐语汇。文章指出其成长经历横跨德班多个城镇，广泛吸收本地节奏模式，形成兼具野性与纪律性的混合声音，被乐评称为'gqom 2.0'或'德班未来之声'。专辑在声音设计上具有鲜明层次，如'MoonWalk Two'中Jersey drill式低音搭配近似Burial的碎木鱼声与失谐lead音，构建紧张感；标题曲与'Emotional Damage'则将祖鲁语人声采样与trance、scratch元素重组，展现出跨类型俱乐部戏剧性。乐评认为尽管gqom近年来同质化倾向明显，但Akiid对新鲜冲击力的追求有效突破了这一局限。

items.body:
Contours follows up an excellent LP for Music From Memory in 2024 with a strong  EP of percussive fancies, full of emotive Motor City pads x resonant drums, tipped FFO Dan Curtin, Workshop, Theo P, early Andy Stott, Gábor Lázár.

Cumbria-raised, Manchester-based Tom Burford’s Contours project was last heard on that Music from Memory ace transitioning into a more contemplative sphere with results comparable to Steve Reich, Richard Skelton, or Alice Coltrane. The 4 tracks here were recorded at around the same time as that LP, but follow an altogether more club-focussed trajectory, most successfully on ‘Sterile Light’ that features a square bassline that mimics Theo P's ‘Heal Yourself and Move’, except with stretched, plastic strings that could have been lifted straight off a theo burt record.

In other words, high praise!
items._cn_summary: Contours项目由Cumbria出身、现居曼彻斯特的Tom Burford操持，此张EP延续其2024年Music From Memory厂牌专辑的脉络，转向更偏俱乐部语境。整张作品以打击乐为核心框架，铺陈底特律风格的情感化合成器pad与共鸣鼓机声响，四首曲目与前作同期录制，但走向更为舞池导向。其中《Sterile Light》一曲表现尤为突出，方形低频线条复刻Theo Parrish名作《Heal Yourself and Move》的质感，再覆以拉伸的塑料感弦乐，巧妙衔接了底特律techno的律动与英式实验电子的内省气质。整体定位介于氛围与俱乐部节拍之间，声音设计细致且具备明确的个人语言，是从内省向律动过渡的一次成功探索。

items.body:
Released in 2017, Dasein was Richard H. Kirk's first solo album in 5 years, recorded by the founding member of Cabaret Voltaire at Western Works, Sheffield, over a three-year period.

"Work began with recording on midi and analogue synthesisers before guitar and vocals (Kirk’s first use of vocals in 10 years) were added. Kirk explains, “A lot of time was spent on post-production, editing and then living with the material and I think it benefited from stepping back and then revisiting after doing other things.”

Although not an overtly political album, it’s hard not to hear a reaction to recent years’ world events in the overwhelming urgency of ‘Nuclear Cloud’ or ‘20 Block Lockdown’ or in ‘New Lucifer / The Truth Is Bad’. When questioned Kirk admits, “It’s not really a political album, but over recent years – during the recording – all manner of horrorshow events have cropped up and now we seem to be in a rerun of the Cold War with Russia back as the Bogeyman.” The album’s title, Dasein (a German word meaning “being there” or “presence”, often translated into English as “existence”), is a fundamental concept in existentialism.

Kirk explains “culture succumbs to nostalgia in much the same way that an individual looks back wistfully to adolescence or childhood - the nostalgia is partly for a time when he or she wasn’t nostalgic, just lived purely IN THE NOW.” In 2014, during the recording period, Kirk began work on Cabaret Voltaire live and so the two projects coexisted in tandem. Although Kirk’s varied projects have always existed separate to one another, says Kirk, “in the past some solo works served as a blueprint for what I did later with Cabaret Voltaire”.

Billed as a performance consisting solely of machines, multi-screen projections and Richard H. Kirk, Cabaret Voltaire recently announced the first UK performance in over 20 years at the Devil’s Arse Cave (aka Peak Cavern) in Castleton, Derbyshire on Saturday 29 April. Kirk will perform entirely new material for a performance relevant to the 21st Century with no nostalgia."
items._cn_summary: Cabaret Voltaire创始成员Richard H. Kirk的2017年专辑《Dasein》耗时三年完成于谢菲尔德的Western Works工作室。录制从midi与模拟合成器起步,后叠加吉他与他十年来首次献声的人声,大量时间投入后期编辑与反复打磨。专辑名义上不直接谈论政治,但曲目如《Nuclear Cloud》《20 Block Lockdown》《New Lucifer / The Truth Is Bad》中弥漫的紧迫感显然映照出近年世界局势的动荡,Kirk本人也承认冷战回潮的氛围渗透了创作。专辑标题取自存在主义德语术语,探讨文化怀旧与活在当下的张力。同期Kirk重启了Cabaret Voltaire的现场演出计划,宣告二十余年来首次英国演出,并强调将以全新素材回应二十一世纪语境,拒绝沉溺于复古情结。

items.body:
'Aeternum (Existenz)' from Dave Sumner, aka Function on Tresor. 

"Much like the fusion resulting in the output of light and heat within a star, the last seven years for Dave Sumner, aka Function, have been defined by immense change and an outpouring of creative energy. What began in late 2016 as a period of burnout from a relentless touring life became a catalyst for the most prolific recording era of his career. At the time, the studio became the only viable escape, a space to transmute exhaustion into a gestalt work.

Aeternum (Existenz) serves as the missing element in this creative arc. It acts as the final chapter of a cycle, that began with the 2019 album Existenz and moved through Subject f (Transcendence), Awakening from the Illusory Self, and Green EP. Drawing inspiration from the seven stages of alchemy, this mini-album represents a cathartic process; a natural end point of a psychological cycle and the beginning of a new curve.

Across the six tracks on the mini-LP, recorded 2016-2019, Function builds a unique world, one which underlines his place as one of the luminaries of contemporary techno.

Opening track, Ascent, traverses the space between ambient and techno; second track City Of Luz almost fades into itself across its twelve minutes before Transmutation brings around a reawakening with a beat that would not have sounded out of place on an early Rephlex or even a Sähko release. Final track on the 12”, Growth Cycle is fittingly a re-version/re-vision of a track on the Existenz LP; Robert Owens’ soulful vocal now Stefanie Parnow's floating Siren-like voice with music that feels reborn: fresh, strong and insistent.

The digital pack contains two further tracks, the deep electro of November 29, as well as Rubedo, a spacial ambient track that feels like the final glowing red embers of a fire turning to ash as the sun rises to reveal a new, golden dawn.

Aeternum (Existenz) is the final chapter of the soundtrack to Function’s spiritual awakening, the closing of a door and the clearing of a path. It’s a sonic manifestation of the Magnum Opus completed, a moment of total integration, where the leaden weight of the journey is finally perfected into the incorruptible gold of the spirit.

It is dedicated to John Mendez, aka Silent Servant, Sumner’s dear friend and lifelong collaborator."
items._cn_summary: 这张迷你专辑是Function七年创作周期的终章，取材自2016至2019年的录音素材，以炼金术七阶段为隐喻，串联此前《Existenz》《Subject f》等作品所构建的精神觉醒叙事。整体游走于氛围与techno之间：开篇在环境音与节奏之间过渡，中段近十二分钟的曲目缓慢消解于自身内部，随后以更偏Rephlex或Sähko厂牌风格的electro节拍带来再觉醒。终曲重新诠释前作，由Stefanie Parnow替代Robert Owens的人声采样，数字版另收录深沉的electro曲与空间氛围作品。整张唱片以厂牌Tresor发行，呈现一种从燃烧到灰烬再到金色黎明的意象转换，是techno制作人将个人精神历程融入作品的典型案例。

items.body:
Steve Rachmad gets his Dekmantel flowers with three trax of bucking, burning, Detroit-styled bangers.

Rachmad’s ‘3-6-9 EP’ appears some 40 years deep into his thing with a trio of analog-sculpted tools for deeper, driving ends of the night. ‘3 Creation Energy’ goes toughest with Suburban Knight-style bassline and bucking claps harnessing a virulent power surge lead that threatens to leap off the grid, whereas ‘6 Physical Manifestation’ settles into a strident square bass groove modulated to pendulous swagger, and ‘9 Completion and Delivery’ proves his jazzy flair for kaotic harmonies and acid Detroit lustre with a Dutch edge.
items._cn_summary: Steve Rachmad 在 Dekmantel 厂牌发行三曲 EP，深入其四十年技艺积累。首曲以坚硬低音线和失序拍手构建强劲张力，配合具有危险感的引线音色；第二曲转向稳定的方波贝斯律动，沉稳而摇摆；终曲展露爵士化的和声感知与酸性底特律光泽，并融入荷兰电子场景的边缘质感。三首曲目均以模拟合成器为核心工具，面向深夜舞池更深、更具驱动力的时段，延续底特律技术派传统的同时保留个人化的声音辨识度。

items.body: Those of a certain age remember when television stations used to sign off for the night. A cheerful TV announcer would share the station identification and a pleasant goodbye, music would play (most often the national anthem) and the station would either display a static image or simply go dark. If this were the only station broadcasting, the person watching would turn off the set, and watch as the lights condensed to a dot before a final pop. Then it was time – really time – to go to bed. Few such stations remain, as the world has shifted to 24/7 access. Michael Branch (Speed of Life) recalls, “There was something magical about it. I (felt) as if I was floating outside of or removed from any notion of time.” In the digital era, it’s hard to imagine hours in which no moving images are available to view, as if nothing of any consequence is unfolding. This set of imaginary sign-off music may evoke nostalgia in older listeners and seem like sci-fi to younger listeners. The clever “Television Set” CD packaging adds to the allure. “KKZ96 (Wonder People”) begins with piano and ethereal chords, as if the mind is soaring into the imagination. As drums are folded in, one thinks of Little Nemo’s Adventures in Slumberland. The mind is left to wonder what events might be unfolding in the in-between time, unrecognized, unreported and most importantly, unbroadcast. And who are the wonder people? Are they a separate race of people active only in the invisible hours, or the images that we miss? The beatless “KCBS (Electric Lights)” dances like its namesake, without the use of percussion. The chords ebb and flow in hypnotic fashion, capturing Branch’s sense of magic. At the time, television was relatively young, and grandparents could remember when they were able to scrape enough money together for their first set: the TV itself was a wonder, a gift. Almost any broadcast seemed magical, as opposed to today, when thousands of options are available yet few possess that early allure. “KHQ6 (Visitor)” has the feel of an early black-and-white film about invaders from Mars, or from the deep, or from the Antarctic. Something otherworldly is already here, and the race is on to get other people to acknowledge their existence. It’s late at night, and Branch’s parents have gone to bed and may or may not know their son is watching; despite the fact that he has seen wonders, he cannot wake them up for fear of being punished. The next piece continues to play upon such fears, albeit gently; the chiming tones both settle and alert, an electronic pulse developing like the lights of a quietly descending spaceship, then fading slowly like a phantasm. The finale, “WTVF,” bridges the gap between the sign-off and the sign-in, hours later; guitar chords are laid atop a mysterious drone as the synthesizers vibrate, the fifteen-minute length creating a trance-like effect. Then at the very end, voices buried in static. The precocious child drifts off to sleep with one salient question on his mind: What’s on TV tomorrow? (Richard Allen)
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑构想的是美国电视台深夜停播时播放的虚拟告别音乐，主题围绕电视消失后那段「无影像时间」的空白感展开。Speed of Life 以钢琴、合成器铺陈空灵的氛围，鼓组的加入唤起类似动画配乐的梦境感；多数曲目以和弦流动和无拍号律动构建催眠效果，部分曲目模拟早期黑白电影中太空入侵者的不安意象，结尾以十五分钟的吉他与合成器嗡鸣桥接停播与清晨开播之间的空白。电视造型的CD包装强化了怀旧与科幻交错的趣味。整体制作呈现出对消失媒介时代的感性追忆，适合喜欢氛围音乐和概念性声音作品的听众。

items.body: Review by kev rowland — Having only recently come across Rob with his excellent 'Overflow' release it seemed fitting to go back a few years and investigate his 2024 debut, 'Explode My Head'. At the time of this release he was playing in both Mascot Moth and The Felix Subway Band, had co-founded Z Machine with Owen Rosser and Gareth Piper, and had been under the wing of Ian East (Gong) for four years to improve his sax playing. On this release Rob provides all guitars, saxophone, bass, vocals & sfx, but he has also brought in a few guests to make this much more of a band release as opposed to a one-man project, including the aforementioned Mr. East who contributes both flute and bass clarinet. The excellent drummer Eliseo Salverri is utilised on most tracks, and it is no surprise that Rob also used his talents on his second album.Rob is very much influenced by British progressive bands who are more experimental than many, with Cardiacs and pronk being very much the major style combined with elements of jazz fusion, Steve Hillage, Gong, Gentle Giant, VDGG, PO90 and others. Sax is sometimes the main musical lead, at others it could be the guitar, or it may even be the voice, one just never knows where this meandering musical journey is going to lead next. Often jagged, never mainstream, this is music which feels as if is from a time gone by when anything was possible with a refusal to conform to what many expect, even within the prog scene. Apparently, Rob was first influenced by guitarist Tony McPhee from The Groundhogs, a band one rarely sees mentioned today, but who released some phenomenal albums (check out 'Thank Christ for the Bomb' and 'Split', both essential), so he has a different starting point to many which undoubtedly has impacted his eccentricity.At the heart of this album is melody, but sometimes that is almost subliminal with chaos all around, yet it always makes sense. Rob is a real artist, one who goes where the muse takes him as opposed to following the herd, which is probably why he decided he needed a video to go with this so spent three frantic months building a set from scratch, making 30+ plasticene figures to inhabit it and then three long weeks of animation (for a total of about a minute and a half of footage!). The cover artwork is taken from this. There is a sense of lightness within this release, yet it refuses to compromise and the result is something which is thoroughly enjoyable indeed, and progheads looking for something a little alternative to the norm will thoroughly enjoy this.
items._genre: experimental prog / Canterbury-influenced / jazz fusion / avant-pop
items._cn_summary: 这是Rob Harrison于2024年发行的首张专辑《Explode My Head》，由本人包揽吉他、萨克斯、贝斯、人声及音效制作，并邀请Ian East（Gong）参与长笛与低音单簧管，鼓手Eliseo Salverri负责大部分曲目打击乐部分。作品深受英国实验前卫影响，融合Cardiacs风格的夸张节奏、jazz fusion元素，以及Steve Hillage、Gong、Gentle Giant、VDGG、PO90等多支乐队的美学。萨克斯、吉他与人声在不同曲目中轮流担任主导，结构尖锐不规则，拒绝任何可预期的形式逻辑。Tony McPhee（The Groundhogs）的吉他风格是其起点，也赋予作品独特的怪异性。专辑在混乱与旋律之间保持张力，所有碎片最终回归完整结构。封面取材自Harrison手工制作的定格动画短片——包含三十多个黏土角色，历时数月完成，体现了创作者的整体艺术理念。整体呈现出独立、不妥协的姿态，对寻求非常规聆听体验的前卫乐迷具有持续吸引力。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — A meeting between guitarist Matt Stevens, drummer Stuart Marshall, and bassist Kevin Feazey, initially intended for recording Stevens' second solo �lbum, led to the formation of the band The Fierce and the Dead; they incorporated progressive elements into stoner rock and post-rock, demonstrating how well these styles blended together. For their second album, they added Steve Cleaton to the permanent lineup on second guitar, while Terry Edwards continued as a guest musician on saxophone and trumpet.Part 4 already starts with notes reminiscent of Robert Fripp, before the distortion kicks in and it follows its own path, a path of distortion, and where atonality will not be foreign. "Ark" creates guitar-driven atmospheres underpinned by drumming that at times recalls Monomyth, while "Let's Start a Cult" feels like postmodern punk rock, featuring guitar work reminiscent of Tom Verlaine from Television. Here, Terry Edwards' saxophone enters the mix, adding a welcome splash of color to the monochromatic landscape.The variety reflected in the album is striking: "Pyramid Hat" is a transcendental psychedelic funk track that bursts through the speakers; the hinted-at Eastern melody gives way to the start of "I Like It, I'm into It," where the bass takes center stage and one of the guitars seems to erupt like Fireworks, yet once those fade, the drums, bass, and a second guitar remain as a trio, continuing to dig deep into the territory where King Crimson collides with Black Sabbath."Spooky Action" sounds powerful, almost industrial, yet suddenly turns vulnerable and sensitive; one of the album's key strengths is that it retains a fresh, jam-session vibe, a sense of playfulness, and at times, its spirit reminded me of the more experimental side of The Flaming Lips."And the Bandit" is a different story: far more complex in structure and progressive, with a Yes-like feel where the ghosts of Chris Squire and Steve Howe seem to appear at times!"Entropy" evokes Adrian Belew collaborating with Toe, a major influence that is palpable throughout the album. "Part 5" revisits the tribute to Fripp, with the saxophone adding a wonderful touch, while "Chief" brings the album to a close with an air of mystery and melancholy; it is a record that shows great promise and delivers, opening doors to future sonic explorations while remaining true to the serendipitous beginnings that brought the band together when they least expected it.
items._genre: post-rock / math rock / progressive / experimental rock
items._cn_summary: The Fierce and the Dead 的第二张专辑《Spooky Action》将后摇滚、数学摇滚与前卫摇滚元素相融合，同时保留stoner rock的厚重感。乐队以双吉他的编制为核心，配合鼓与贝斯构建层次丰富的音墙，萨克斯与喇叭的加入为作品增添了独特的色彩变化。专辑展现出强烈的实验意识：从无调性的失真段落、东方旋律的暗示，到带有King Crimson与Black Sabbath碰撞感的riff，再到Fripp式的吉他语汇与Yes般的复杂结构，听众可在其中感受到Jam session的自由氛围与即兴精神。失真与敏感的脆弱段落交替出现，部分曲目带有工业的力量感与迷幻的跨维度气质，结尾在神秘而忧郁的氛围中收束。整体而言，这是一张在类型融合上颇具野心的作品，对前卫与实验音乐爱好者具有一定的吸引力。

items.body: Brooklyn synth duo Observation Room have spent the last few years finding the heart beating inside the machine. On Superstructure, their debut full-length for à La Carte Records, Marina F and Chloe Olson expand the hypnotic precision of their self-titled EP into something stranger, warmer, and more textural: synth-pop with its circuitry exposed and the windows cracked open. The record keeps the duo’s precise electronic chill intact, but fattens it with breath, doubt, humour, and a bright ache that makes you suspect the machines have been listening while you talk in your sleep. Observation Room have made synth-pop with blood pressure: bright surfaces, nervous systems, and a brain full of alarms. Superstructure is smart, strange, physical, and wide awake, grinning hard under the emergency lights. The first single, Running Lights, works as both invitation and warning flare. It locks into a headlight-after-headlight momentum, steady enough for the dance floor but too keyed-up to dissolve into lifestyle wallpaper. The pulse is sleek, but not passive; every repetition seems to tighten the room by a few degrees. When the chorus finally opens, it feels earned, like a locked stairwell suddenly giving onto sky. Running Lights draws its charge from the duo’s devotion to process, pressure, and disciplined play. The reference points are clear enough: Depeche Mode’s severe romance, Book of Love’s gloss, OMD’s machine-pop manners, plus older electronic cousins from krautrock, Tangerine Dream, and early Human League. But Observation Room are not simply arranging their influences into a tasteful mood board. They keep their hands on the method. They build small systems, repeat them, compress them, and wait for strange colours to leak out. Listen to Running Lights below. Superstructure arrives September 11. Pre-order here. Superstructure by Observation Room The album’s title, Superstructure, carries a clean, glassy double charge. On one side is architecture: the frame, the scaffold, the built environment. On the other is ideology: the unseen system that tells the body where to move, what to fear, and how to behave. Across the LP, private panic keeps finding its public wiring. Surveillance begins as a twitch behind the eyes, then expands into policy, screens, money, cops, bosses, feeds, and all the little invisible rails that teach people where to stand. Marina F and Olson, sharpened by political organizing and dread, treat anxiety not as a personal defect but as something manufactured, maintained, and, in certain flashes, danced through. The production, handled and mixed by Marina F in Brooklyn, gives the record depth, pressure, and enough space for its uglier textures to breathe. Mechanical bloops, field recordings, dissonant corners, and thick low-end touches from 90s house press against vocal harmonies shaped by rooms full of bodies. The result is both intimate and civic, club-lit and fluorescent, as if the songs were built for headphones, basement speakers, and the nervous walk home afterward. Sharon Aiza Engel’s mastering gives the album firm edges without draining its glow. Follow Observation Room: Instagram Bandcamp Photo: Tim O’Connell The post Brooklyn Synthpop Duo Observation Room Share New Single “Running Lights” — Debut Album “Superstructure” Announced! appeared first on Post-Punk.com.
items._cn_summary: 布鲁克林合成器二人组Observation Room的首张专辑《Superstructure》由Marina F与Chloe Olson共同创作，在à La Carte Records发行。专辑在保持电子冷感与催眠式精度的同时，融入了呼吸感、疑虑与幽默，形成有体温的合成器流行。制作由Marina F在布鲁克林完成，机械音效、田野录音、不和谐音色与九十年代浩室低音并行，辅以具身体感的和声编排。受Depeche Mode、OMD、Book of Love及Krautrock影响，但以政治组织经验为底色，将焦虑视为被制造的产物而非个人缺陷。首支单曲《Running Lights》以重复脉冲构建张力，副歌展开如楼梯通向天空。专辑探讨监控、意识形态与公共恐惧的隐性架构。

items.album: SEKTION release first album ‘Druck’ on Geometrik Records
items.excerpt: SEKTION, the project of German electronic musicians AtomTM (Uwe Schmidt) and Siegmar Fricke, release “Druck“, their first full-length album, on Geometrik Records, out 17 July 2026 as a limited black vinyl LP of 250 copies. The record moves through industrial and experimental electronic territory across thirteen tracks and marks the first official SEKTION collaboration between the two, a connection the pair trace back to 1992. SEKTION detail ‘Druck’ and its structure &#822
items.body: SEKTION, the project of German electronic musicians AtomTM (Uwe Schmidt) and Siegmar Fricke, release “Druck“, their first full-length album, on Geometrik Records, out 17 July 2026 as a limited black vinyl LP of 250 copies. The record moves through industrial and experimental electronic territory across thirteen tracks and marks the first official SEKTION collaboration between the two, a connection the pair trace back to 1992. SEKTION detail ‘Druck’ and its structure “Druck” is built from four compositional frameworks that Schmidt and Fricke title Vokostasis, Digitraktion, Leerzeichen and Unwucht. The thirteen tracks follow those groups in sequence: four “Vokostasis” pieces and four “Digitraktion” pieces on the first side, then two “Leerzeichen” edits and three “Unwucht” edits on the second. The duo shape metallic textures, granular rhythms and slow structural shifts, with frequency-altered voice fragments and layers of tape noise running through the record. Geometrik Records has posted four excerpts from the album on SoundCloud. The album is the first SEKTION full-length. It follows “Kopplung”, a two-track SEKTION release issued in May 2025. Geometrik Records is the Madrid label associated with Spanish industrial group Esplendor Geométrico. About SEKTION SEKTION pairs Uwe Schmidt and Siegmar Fricke, two German artists whose work reaches back to the late 1980s and early 1990s. Schmidt, born on 27 August 1968 in Frankfurt am Main, has recorded prolifically since 1988 under names that include Atom TM, Atom Heart, Lassigue Bendthaus and Señor Coconut. He co-founded the label Rather Interesting with Pete Namlook and has released through Raster-Noton, Fax and Mille Plateaux, among others. His work ranges across techno, ambient, industrial and electrolatino, and his Señor Coconut album “El Baile Alemán” (2000) reworked Kraftwerk as Latin dance music. As a producer and remixer he has worked with Ryuichi Sakamoto, Haruomi Hosono of Yellow Magic Orchestra, Depeche Mode, Merzbow and Towa Tei, and he has reconstructed and remixed material by Esplendor Geométrico. In July 2024, Uwe H. Schmidt headlined the Russian Outline festival, which returned after its last edition in 2016, and this amid the ongoing conflict with Ukraine. It didn’t take long before critics, such as Ukrainian activist Maya Baklanova, rightfully said that Western artists performing in Russia were normalizing the war and supporting the Russian regime by their participation. Siegmar Fricke began experimenting with shortwave radio and acoustic noise around 1981, in the space between musique concrète and post-industrial sound, and became an active figure in the international cassette-culture network. He ran his own label, Bestattungsinstitut, and issued numerous tapes between 1985 and 1993 spanning experimental music, EBM and ambient. Since the 2000s he has worked mainly as Pharmakustik, and his collaborations include work with Conrad Schnitzler and Maurizio Bianchi. “Druck” brings the two together as SEKTION for their first album, extending a working relationship the pair date to 1992.
items._cn_summary: SEKTION首张全长专辑《Druck》由德国电子音乐人AtomTM（Uwe Schmidt）与Siegmar Fricke合作完成，经马德里厂牌Geometrik Records发行限量黑胶。整张唱片横跨十三首曲目，按四个作曲框架Vokostasis、Digitraktion、Leerzeichen与Unwucht顺序编排，以金属质感音色、颗粒化节奏、缓慢的结构位移为核心，辅以频率变形的人声碎片与磁带噪音层叠。两人自1992年起便有合作渊源，此作是首张正式联合专辑。此前Fricke主要以Pharmakustik名义活跃，Schmidt则以AtomTM等多重身份长期涉足实验电子领域，曾与Ryuichi Sakamoto、Merzbow等合作。专辑在Geometrik Records的工业血统中延续了对实验声响与暗潮张力的探索。

items.body: British electro-industrial group Portion Control have released “Tex-Mex (Live at Dolce Vita, Lausanne 6/12/85)“, the second single from their archival box set “1983-86 – Hit The Pulse to Purge…“, out 14 August 2026 on Artoffact Records. The set collects the London group’s mid-1980s work across a 4xCD box, a digital edition and a limited red vinyl LP. You can stream and pre-order the box set through the Bandcamp player below. 1983-86 – Hit The Pulse to Purge… by Portion Control Portion Control detail ‘Tex-Mex’ and the box set “Tex-Mex” was recorded in December 1985 at the Dolce Vita in Lausanne, a Swiss venue that had opened earlier that year, and the performance was filmed. The band trace the track back to their studio sessions of the period rather than the stage. “‘Tex-Mex’ was recorded as part of the ‘..Step Forward’ recording sessions at Guerilla Studios in Little Venice, London,” the band recall. “It was where William Orbit had his recording base at the time and we utilised a lot of the equipment he had set up there for his own early electronic work.” A video for the single accompanies the release. The box set, “1983-86 – Hit The Pulse to Purge…”, gathers 77 tracks. It brings together the 1983 mini-LP “Hit The Pulse”, the albums “..Step Forward” (1984) and “Psycho Bod Saves The World” (1986), the 12-inch singles “The Great Divide”, “Go-Talk” and “Raise The Pulse”, and the “Purge” EP (1986), alongside B-sides, compilation tracks, rarities, remixes, demos and two live recordings, from Amsterdam in 1984 and Lausanne in 1985. Paul Lavigne remastered all 77 tracks at Kontrast Mastering; 16 are previously unreleased and a further 12 appear on CD and digital for the first time. The 4xCD edition comes in a five-panel ecopak with a 24-page booklet designed by Stefan Alt of Ant-Zen, and the red vinyl LP carries ten key tracks. “Tex-Mex” follows “Refugee”, a version reworked by Rhys Fulber of Front Line Assembly that Portion Control issued as the first single in June 2026. The reissue campaign continues the group’s move to Artoffact, which began when Portion Control joined Artoffact Records and released the “SEED EP3.1” EP in December 2025. About Portion Control Portion Control formed in London in 1979 and built a raw, minimal sound around sequenced synthesisers, samplers and strident vocals. Their early records – the 1982 debut album “I Staggered Mentally”, the “Hit The Pulse” mini-LP (1983) and the second album “..Step Forward” (1984) – placed them among the pioneers of hard-edged electronic dance music, and the group supported Depeche Mode on tour in 1984. Their use of early sampling and drum-machine technology fed into the work of later acts including Nitzer Ebb, Skinny Puppy, Front Line Assembly, Nine Inch Nails and Orbital. After a hiatus that began in the late 1980s, Portion Control returned in 2004 with “Wellcome”, followed by “Filthy White Guy” (2006), “Pure Form” (2012) and the run of “SEED” EPs between 2020 and 2025. The group signed to Artoffact Records in late 2025, and the label is now reissuing their catalogue as a series of box sets. “1983-86 – Hit The Pulse to Purge…” is the first of those sets, and “Tex-Mex” is the second single drawn from it.
items._cn_summary: 英国电子工业团体Portion Control即将通过Artoffact厂牌发行1983至86年间作品的档案合集，收录77首曲目，横跨4张CD、数码版及限量红胶LP版本。内容涵盖其1983年迷你专辑、两张录音室专辑、多首12寸单曲及EP，并附带B面曲目、合辑作品、稀有版本、混音、 demo及两段现场录音。'Tex-Mex'作为第二支单曲发布，录制于1985年瑞士洛桑Dolce Vita演出，原始录音在William Orbit驻扎的Guerilla Studios完成，乐队利用其早期电子音乐制作设备。Paul Lavigne在Kontrast Mastering完成全部77首曲目的母带处理，其中16首为首次发行。Reissue计划延续了乐队自2025年12月加入Artoffact以来的合作，首支单曲为Rhys Fulber重新混音的'Refugee'。该团被视为硬核电子舞曲先锋，其早期采样与鼓机运用影响了后续众多艺人。

items.body: Veteran Raymond Watts has continued to reinvent himself for nearly four decades, and this year he returned with the new full-length album “Hurt People Hurt”, delivering ten powerful new tracks. “Hurt People Hurt” sounds exactly as we’ve come to expect from PIG: hard-hitting and relentless, yet always crafted with sophistication and an undeniable sense of melody. The songs are driven by menacing guitars that effortlessly bridge the worlds of Industrial and Metal, while Electronic textures add depth, atmosphere, and an occasional touch of accessibility. One of PIG’s greatest strengths has always been its choruses, and this album is no exception. They are bold, infectious, and anthemic—made to be sung, shouted, danced, and jumped along to. To my ears, PIG still shares a sonic kinship with KMFDM, although fans of Marilyn Manson will undoubtedly find plenty to appreciate here as well. Yet Raymond Watts has always maintained his own unmistakable identity, balancing aggression and provocation with theatrical flair and memorable songwriting. “Hurt People Hurt” is an outstanding album packed with consistently strong material. There isn’t a weak moment to be found, making it genuinely difficult to single out a favorite track. Respect! (Rating:8½). The album was previewed by two singles, “Tosca’s Kiss” and “Sex & Suicide”. Listen to “Sex & Suicide”: Sex & Suicide by PIG About PIG PIG is the long-running industrial rock project of English musician Raymond Watts. Watts launched the project in the late 1980s after earlier work with KMFDM, Einstürzende Neubauten, Psychic TV, Foetus, Schaft, and Schwein. The first PIG release was “A Poke in the Eye… with a Sharp Stick” in 1988. It was followed by “Praise the Lard” in 1991, “A Stroll in the Pork” in 1992, “The Swining” in 1993, “Sinsation” in 1995, “Wrecked” in 1996, and “Genuine American Monster” in 1999. After “Pigmartyr” in 2004, released under Watts name and later reissued as “Pigmata”, the project returned with “The Gospel” in 2016, “Risen” in 2018, “Candy” in 2019, “Pain Is God” in 2020, “The Merciless Light” in 2022, and “Red Room” in 2024. The “Feast of Agony” EP followed in 2024, the remastered “Wrecked” in 2025, the remix set “The Merciful Night” in 2025, and now “Hurt People Hurt” in 2026. Current members are Raymond Watts, En Esch, Steve White, and Bradley Bills. Watts remains the core figure, while Jim Davies continues as a key writing collaborator.
items._cn_summary: Raymond Watts 携新专辑《Hurt People Hurt》回归，延续了 PIG 项目近四十年的工业摇滚路线。专辑收录十首作品，以凶猛的吉他为骨架，横跨工业与金属领域，同时融入电子音色以增加层次感和氛围渲染。副歌部分是这张专辑的亮点，大胆且具有感染力，适合现场合唱与舞动。与 KMFDM 共享相似的工业血脉，又因戏剧化的舞台感和挑衅性而区别于 Marilyn Manson 式的主流路线。歌曲创作兼具攻击性与旋律性，每一首作品都保持了较高水准，难以挑出明显的弱点。两支先行单曲《Tosca's Kiss》和《Sex & Suicide》为专辑预热。整体而言，这是一张成熟的工业摇滚作品，在类型框架内展现了持续的创造力与辨识度。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由贝斯手乔·莫里斯领衔，联合罗布·布朗、安娜·韦伯与马修·鲁索组成四重奏，以抗议音乐为切入点展开即兴创作。两位萨克斯/长笛手与贝斯、鼓的组合延续了自由爵士的核心语汇——非预设的结构、开放式的互动、以及对音色的持续探索。莫里斯在文案中将作品置于当下社会语境之中，使音乐超越了纯粹的声响实验，带有明确的政治表态意味。专辑由波兰独立厂牌Fundacja Słuchaj发行，延续了该厂牌对前卫即兴音乐的一贯支持。然而由于原乐评内容极为简短，仅触及专辑的创作动机与编制信息，缺少对具体演奏技法、录音质量或作品结构的深入分析，因此无法对其艺术完成度做出更充分的判断。整体而言，这是一张带有社会议题意识的前卫爵士即兴作品，适合关注自由即兴与实验音乐的听众进一步了解。

items.body: Review by kev rowland — This compilation is designed to provide an overview of Space Debris, a still active Krautrock band from Germany. Three of the nine tracks on the triple vinyl set from FdeM, which is already sold out by the way, are more than 20 minutes long while the set is more than two hours in length. If you can find a copy it also comes with a 24 pp A4 booklet, although you may find it easier to search out the digital version which also has two additional numbers. Formed in 2002 by two friends, Tommy Gorny (guitar) and Christian J�ger (drums), to play improvised music inspired by the Seventies' Krautrock and Psychedelic bands, they were joined by keyboard player Winnie Rimbach-Sator in 2008 and have had a few bassists, although Vroni Frisch has been there for the last decade. However, this material predates her arrival, stretching all the way back to 2005, with "Villamountain" hailing from 2012 and is the only previously unreleased material.I had not heard of this band prior to receiving the album, but I don't feel too bad given that label boss and Krautrock connoisseur Keith Jones only came across them about a year ago. The compilation was put together by the band themselves and shows that while they may be more underground than most, that is not down to lack of ability. Given this is generally improvised it is interesting to hear just how direct and together this album is and feels far more structured than many of the live composition works I come across. Gorny is often the lead melody, the keyboards are there to provide counterpoint and something to work against, the bass is the warmth glue which keeps it all together and then there are drums which are much more like a lead instrument in their own right as opposed to "just" holding it all together.They have been likened to the spirit of early Deep Purple (think "Mandrake Root"), Hendrix, Pink Floyd and Can while others have pointed towards 'Bitches Brew', and there is certainly a heavier relationships with bands like these as opposed to �resund Space Collective which is more dramatically Space Rock in nature. This is a fascinating album which deserves to be listened to on headphones when one has the time to really get inside what is going on, and fans of Krautrock certainly need to discover these guys if they have yet to come across them.

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑是对德国Krautrock乐队Space Debris演出生涯的回顾，收录九首作品，总时长超过两小时，其中三首超过二十分钟。乐队由两位好友于2002年创立，最初以即兴演奏为目标，受七十年代Krautrock与迷幻摇滚影响，后加入键盘手和贝斯手完成编制。专辑素材跨越2005至2012年，展示了乐队在键盘与吉他之间构建对抗性旋律的方式，以及鼓手作为主导性乐器而非单纯节奏支撑的处理手法。评论指出其结构感比多数现场即兴专辑更为清晰紧凑，在Deep Purple、Jimi Hendrix、Pink Floyd、Can乃至Miles Davis《Bitches Brew》的气质之间找到平衡点。作为独立地下厂牌的小众再版，已售罄并附有实体手册，具有一定的收藏价值，适合有充裕时间且熟悉该脉络的听众深入聆听。

items.body: Dirk Da Davo will forever be associated with The Neon Judgement, the legendary Belgian band that remains a benchmark and a source of inspiration for countless artists and fans. It was therefore quite a challenge when Dirk released the debut album of his new project, Neon Electronics, In 1999. While it never quite achieved the same level of recognition as The Neon Judgement, it is fair to say that, particularly in its early years, the project sounded both innovative and visionary. Twenty-six years later, the EP/mini-album “Liberation” was released and immediately announced as Neon Electronics’ final new production. The band—which for many years featured Glenn Keteleer and Pieter-Jan Theunis alongside Dirk Da Davo—had decided to call it a day. Over the course of a quarter-century, Neon Electronics built up an impressive body of work. Their original Techno-EBM sound gradually evolved, and “Liberation” ultimately brings the story full circle, returning to where it all began for Dirk: 80s influences transformed into strong, memorable songs infused with a powerful sense of nostalgia. Released by the Spanish label Oráculo Records, the record strikes me as a compelling sonic epitaph. I spoke with Dirk Da Davo about this final chapter, but our conversation explored much more besides. (Picture credits by Patrice Hoerner / Interview courtesy by Inferno Sound Diaries) Liberation by NEON ELECTRONICS Dirk Da Davo / Neon Electronics interview Q: Hi Dirk, I’d actually like to start with what might otherwise have been the last question of this interview: what now? What else would you still like to achieve musically? Dirk: That’s an interesting question to start with! I look back and feel satisfied with a musical career of 45 years. I am happy to have had the top of my career in a time when the Electro-Punk and Rock & Roll level was still significantly higher in the music scene. I have travelled around the world, played in amazing locations and had the opportunity to collaborate with some very talented musicians. For example, the collaboration with my childhood hero Jean-Marie Aerts under DDDJMX is something I’m very proud of. Also a lot of fun, more recently, was the remix I made for Luc Van Acker, as well as my solo releases. What I never did before, and so still to be achieved, is composing music for a movie. I still would like to do that. So yes, they can call me 🙂 Q: The announcement of the end of Neon Electronics came as a surprise to me. Had you seen this coming for a while, and what ultimately influenced your decision? Dirk: I started collaborating with Glenn Keteleer (aka Radical G) 15 years ago. A few years later Pieter-Jan Theunis joined us on bass guitar. I enjoyed working and playing with these guys a lot. The decision to stop the project has grown over the last year. We decided to make one final album, but it had to be a good one. And so, we started working on the final Neon Electronics EP “Liberation” which got released recently. The album is the perfect harmony between 3 talented musicians, with each their own unique style and therefore in my opinion a very interesting and very good album. Q: I think it’s fair to say that you have always had a critical perspective on the evolution of music. Just consider the decline of the physical format, the rise of digitalization and streaming platforms, the abundance of software to make music, and now the growing presence of AI and social media. How do you view these developments with all your experience, to what extent did they influence your decision to stop Neon Electronics, and might they also affect the continuation of your musical career? Dirk: It is true that I am not known for my optimism 🙂 And a critical perspective has simply been part of my education, influenced and stimulated by my late father. I will never lose my critical view on music, nor on society in general. It is the essence of my personality, and it has always affected my musical style. For sure, these changes, how the music scene has evolved, by some defined as progress, by others as destruction, have played a part in the decision to close the Neon Electronics chapter. Do not understand me wrongly, I will keep on making music, music is my therapy. But let’s say that I am happy not to be an 18-year-old musician at the start of his career who needs to compete with soulless AI music, and whose success is measured in the quantity of likes on social media. Q: When you started out as a young musician in the early 1980s, Electronic music and its accompanying underground scene were a genuine phenomenon—something many people who experienced it still look back on with nostalgia, and perhaps even longing. How do you look back on that era? And is there still such a thing as a true underground scene today, or is everything now measured by streaming numbers, sales figures, algorithms, and increasingly standardized expectations? Dirk: The eighties were so interesting from a creative point of view. You had all these cult labels like 4AD, Factory Records, Les Disques Du Crépuscule, and many more, releasing vinyl after vinyl with interesting and often obscure music. There was an opportunity to be experimental, to think out of the box, and that’s how some of the best music of all times has been born. For the artists at the time, these labels created perspective; these times it was still possible to launch a career from the very deep underground scene. An underground scene or a countermovement will always exist. Nothing makes me happier than discovering music from young Punky musicians. Last week I received a message from a 15-year-old very cool girlie bass player. She said The Neon Judgment still is an inspiration for her play. This fills me with hope. Q: The first Neon Electronics release dates back to 1999. How do you look back on a journey that lasted more than a quarter of a century, and what are the highs and lows that immediately come to mind? Dirk: The year 1999 was a turning point in my musical career. It was year I started my own label DancedelicD, with the help of some cyber-IT punks. It also was the year that Neon Electronics was born. Did you know that the first Neon Electronics concert (@ Rumba, Leuven, Belgium – 1999) has been streamed Live on the Internet? This was quite revolting at the time, and the path towards independency had been set. The Neon Electronics journey has been interesting, it gave me the freedom to explore new boundaries, to try some different styles, to collaborate with different artists, … Q: How difficult—or perhaps how easy—was it to launch a new project after spending so many years with the legendary The Neon Judgement, especially considering that the new project’s name still contained a reference to it? Dirk: This has not always been easy, especially in the beginning. I wanted to re-build my own musical identity, and in a certain way liberate myself from the ubiquitous expectations connected to the name The Neon Judgement. Choosing the difficult way has always been my style: -) But at the same time, I wanted to stay loyal to my fans, and therefore the Neon referral stayed in Neon Electronics. Like Neon with a twist, you don’t always know what to expect. Q: Neon Electronics went through several different phases in terms of influences and line-up, which also resulted in albums that could sound quite distinct from one another. What did this project represent for you in terms of artistic expression, musical influences, and personal evolution? Dirk: Indeed, over the last 25 years Neon Electronics has known different line-ups. As an artist I feel the need to step out of the safety zone and to try something new. Back in the days I was experimenting with a new way of bringing live music, like a semi-DJ-set with live instruments and vocals. During the 90s I went clubbing a lot, which had its influence on Neon Electronics, back then you could feel its connection with Techno and sometimes even with House music or, Dance music in general. A few years later I felt again like playing in a band, and that resulted in the actual line-up with Glenn and PJ. Neon Electronics – Press photo 2019 Q: When you started Neon Electronics, I had the distinct feeling that you were doing something innovative, something that could also be heard at the time in the work of artists such as The Hacker, Terence Fixmer, David Carretta, The Horroris ao. Looking back, how innovative do you think it really was? Dirk: Thank you for the compliment. Indeed, freedom and innovation were definitely the driving forces at the start of Neon Electronics. Being different and being independent. This Electro-Punk attitude can be heard very clearly in the first Neon Electronics album. Q: Earlier this year, you released the EP/mini album “Liberation”, which I consider one of your strongest works in years. It combines influences that reach back to the roots of the 80s while presenting them within a contemporary sound. What did you still want to express with this release, and did you already know at the time that these would be the final songs of the project? Dirk: We are also very happy about the way “Liberation” turned out. It reflects how we are and how we want to be as artists. We respect our 80s background but chose for a contemporary sound. Yes, we knew that it would be our final release while creating the songs. The album was meant to be a crossover between Dark-Wave and modern beats, I think we succeeded quite well. Glenn did a great production job, and PJ’s contributions are always amazing. The remixed work from Patrick Codeyns (Front 242) and the Techno remix from Ancient Methods are a nice extra. Q: If you had to choose one Neon Electronics song at this very moment that best represents the project for you, which one would it be, and why? Dirk: It is too difficult to choose only one! They are all my babies. Because the different styles and different line-ups reflect me as an artist, I would choose one from the very beginning and one of our recent works: “Total Wam Bam” (“Neon Electronics”, 1999) & “Justification Unknown” (“Liberation”, 2026). About Neon Electronics Neon Electronics is a Belgian electro-wave and EBM project led by Dirk Da Davo, born Dirk Timmermans, co-founder of The Neon Judgement. The project started in 1999 as a solo project after Da Davo’s work with The Neon Judgement, the Leuven band he formed in 1981 with Frank Vloeberghs, also known as TB Frank. Neon Electronics was created as a separate outlet for electronic dance music. DancedelicD, the label founded by Dirk, describes the project as “electronic dance music without being specific house or techno”. The project’s sound moved between electro-wave, EBM, technoid electronics, post-punk references and guitar-based material. In a 2019 Side-Line interview, Da Davo said: “With Neon Electronics everything is possible, no limits, all freedom!” The first Neon Electronics release was the self-titled album “Neon Electronics” in 1999. “System Rivièra” followed in 2003, with “Swingers Delight” released in 2004 as a live recorded DJ mix CD. The project continued with “Monkey Ever After” in 2006 and “Ever After Monkey” in 2007. “Better Way EP”, a collaboration with The Hacker, was issued in 2009, while “Keylogger” followed in 2012. “Toyboy EP” appeared in 2013, and “Ne” was released in 2015. The project later developed from Da Davo’s solo format into a trio. Glenn Keteleer, also known as Radical G, joined the project during the 2010s, while Pieter-Jan Theunis joined on bass around 2014/2015. By the time of “Apollo”, the lineup was Dirk Da Davo on guitar and vocals, Glenn Keteleer on electronics and vocals, and Pieter-Jan Theunis on bass guitar. “Apollo” was released on April 12, 2019, through DanceDelic-D in co-production with Wool-E Discs. Neon Electronics also worked with Oráculo Records. “Mondriaan” was released as a limited vinyl EP in January 2019, ahead of “Apollo”. The project returned with a rework of The Neon Judgement track “Factory Walk” in December 2024, followed by “Nothing For Nothing” in July 2025 and “Justification Unknown” in February 2026. In 2026, Oráculo Records released “Liberation”, described by the label as “the final chapter in the journey of Dirk Da Davo”. The release featured Dirk Da Davo, Glenn Keteleer and Pieter-Jan Theunis, with remixes by Ancient Methods and Patrick Codenys of Front 242. The digital edition included eight tracks, while the limited 12-inch vinyl edition was pressed in 300 copies.
items._cn_summary: 本文是一篇以Neon Electronics终幕EP《Liberation》为契机的人物访谈侧记，带有回顾与告别性质。文章描述了这个由The Neon Judgement核心成员Dirk Da Davo发起的项目，自1999年首作以来以Techno-EBM为根基，历经二十六年，逐步融入80年代新浪潮影响，形成兼具怀旧感与记忆点的合成器流行化表达。最终EP由西班牙厂牌Oráculo Records发行，被定位为一份声学墓志铭。访谈未深入技术层面，而是借终曲之名探讨音乐生涯的满足与遗憾、对AI时代音乐场景的抗拒，以及尚未实现的电影配乐理想。整体而言，文章以采访为主、音乐分析为辅，透露的是一段比利时暗潮—EBM场景中的尾声叙事。

items.body:
Ana Roxanne’s gorgeous third album, one that finds her ditching the muted, Grouper-like ambience of her earlier work in favour of more sparse, exposed recordings and arrangements that come hugely tipped if yr into Eliana Glass, Susanna Wallumrød, Ethel Cain...

We called Roxanne's last Kranky outing, 2020's effervescent 'Because of a Flower', a "modern classic" - and 'Poem 1' is even stronger. Where its predecessor worked as a cryptonostalgic dream diary, sketching her various component parts - her early obsession with R&B, her introduction to Hindustani music, her life as a jazz hopeful and her college-era fixation on Alice Coltrane - into a surreal, multi-dimensional image, 'Poem 1' is a clean break, or at the very least the beginning of a new era. Her old influences still haunt the backdrop, but Roxanne's third album (if you count her brief but popular debut '~~~') is very much about the present, specifically the days and months that followed a breakup. Rather than wallow in self-pity, Roxanne uses the opportunity to reveal herself fully for the first time, stripping her music of its most tangible aesthetic signifiers to allow her voice to show its most affecting vulnerabilities. So there's no more looping and barely a lick of reverb, yet her voice still soars, accompanied by the simplest instrumentation.

She needs little more than a frozen string drone on 'The Age of Innocence' as she introduces herself again six years after the fact, not as broken pieces but a bold, unwavering voice that cuts through the noise (and pain) of existence. It's a revelation; the motivation has always been there in her music, hidden beneath the repetitions and gestures, and now we witness the fuller picture. "Wild wind blowing / A song playing over the air," she calls out on 'Berceuse in A-flat Minor, Op. 45', playing dimly-lit piano phrases as she sings. "Don't go, don't go." You can imagine being perched at the back of a lounge somewhere late at night, nursing a whiskey while watching Roxanne pour out her heart. Calling it Lynchian might be too close to the bone, but there's always been an air of Julee Cruise's haunted dream-pop hanging in the atmosphere and it wafts to the surface here, bathing Roxanne's words in blue light and stage smoke. "Oh I can never reach you / So I'll keep a piece beside me," she weeps solemnly on 'Keepsake'. "I'll hold it like a jewel, I'll carry the air." 

With these heartbreakers in the rearview, the album's centerpiece 'Untitled II' still hits like a brick to the jaw. Bohren-style doomed, jazzy drums brush away in the background and Roxanne's voice does all the emotional heavy-lifting at half speed. “Losing what I had," she sings, exacting a torturous look at the aftermath of a love lost. The piano and strings help lubricate the movement, but there's nothing to distract us from her words, punctuating them with sluggish, minor key stabs. Crushing and beautiful, it's one of the year's first unquestionable highlights - buy on sight, basically.
items._genre: ambient / dream-pop / experimental vocal / contemporary folk
items._cn_summary: Ana Roxanne的第三张专辑是一次重要的转型之作。她舍弃了此前Grouper式的朦胧氛围质感，转向更稀疏、更裸露的录音与编曲策略，仅以弦乐长音、钢琴短句和极简打击乐为背景，几乎完全依赖人声的脆弱质感来承载情感重量。专辑围绕一段感情结束后的心碎展开，歌词意象私人化且具体，从窗边独坐的画面到关于宝石与空气的哀歌，呈现出一种夜间酒吧独白式的内省氛围。制作上明显剥离了循环结构和混响的修饰，让声音更接近赤裸状态，Julee Cruise式的梦幻流行气质与东方音乐元素隐约浮现于背景。整体而言是一张偏向情绪表达而非声学实验的作品，在个人情感叙事层面有独特深度，但在实验性和跨领域融合上相对克制。

items.body:
Smacking that sweetspot between grime, techno, bassline and soca, Anthoney J Hart (East Man, Imaginary Forces) aka Basic Rhythm delivers a full-bore pack of rampers for Bristol-via-Berlin’s bassbin overlords, Sneaker Social Club.

Active in a vein of uchronic, ‘nuum-bending invention since the 2010’s, but with roots reaching back to ‘90s pirate radio, Hart’s decade-straddling steez yields the crankiest horsepower as Basic Rhythm on ‘8 Bar Techno’. Hewing hard to the brief, he dissects and recombines styles & patterns with a fiercely upfront quality, trampling on putative borders with a rudeboy alacrity that works a treat on up-for -it ‘floors.

The durable torsion of OG jungle tekno and its myriad derivations are twisted into tensile girders, variously splitting the difference between 4/4 grime and hard groove techno in ‘the title tune, or panel-beating sublow into rictus bashiness on ‘Weed Killer’, while firing killer rounds of vocal cuts including the dancehall-grime of ‘Vibez’ with NyNy, or electroid drill with Lyrical Strally and Eklipse.

Along with the precision-tooled rufige of ‘Kонец века’ with Moscow Legend, the mutant soca gallop o ‘Ice cold’, and diesel-fuelled grime-techno of ‘More Pricks than Kicks’, or the dive-bombing darkness of ‘The Deluge’, it’s a hard set for discerning 140BPM shotters, and surely one of Basic Rhythm’s deadliest.
items._genre: grime / techno / bassline / jungle / experimental electronic
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Anthoney J Hart以Basic Rhythm名义发表的最新作品，融合了grime、techno、bassline与soca等多种风格，体现了其跨越十年的音乐脉络。Hart将九十年代pirate radio的根源与当代俱乐部场景结合，对既有类型进行拆解与重组，4/4 grime、硬groove techno、jungle tekno的力道在曲目中交织。专辑邀请多位说唱艺人合作，包括NyNy的dancehall-grime、Lyrical Strally与Eklipse的electroid drill，以及Moscow Legend参与的rufige风格作品。整体制作以140BPM的高速节奏和低频冲击为主轴，标题曲和'Weed Killer'等曲目展现出强力的舞池取向，'The Deluge'则呈现更具暗色的质感。作为Bristol与柏林厂牌Sneaker Social Club的发行，这是为discerning舞池而设计的硬派作品。

items.body:
The crown jewel of German duo Donna Regina's pre-Karaoke Kalk run, 'Follow the Sea' laid out the template for their best known albums, muddling electro-pop with exotica, dub and lounge and inhabiting the liminal zone between Julee Cruise and Saint Etienne.

Regina and Günther Janssen had already released three albums before 'Follow the Sea' arrived, and it was around this time that their music had begun to creep beyond Germany's borders. Matthew Herbert had issued the title track on his Lowlife imprint, bumping it up with his own remix and within a couple of years, Donna Regina had been snapped up by Karaoke Kalk, where they remained for their next umpteen full-lengths. And although each album is more or less the same, there's no other band who makes music quite like this. Regina's voice sounds pitch perfect here, calling over Günther's Kraftwerk-inspired synths on the lengthy 'Jungle' and hissing across a cheeky sample of Aphex Twin's 'Alberto Basalm' on 'Something Happy'.

It's pop music, but the kind of low-key, literate pop that no longer exists, crafted by two heads who clearly love music so much that they've been exhaustively jotting down their findings since 1992. And it's the duo's lack of consistent boundaries that keeps us coming back; they're able to lurch from dubby Americana ('Follow the Sea') to d&b ('Smile') and then try on some ritualistic 'My Life in the Bush of Ghosts' percussive experimentation - and it all sounds as if it's coming from the same honest space.
items._cn_summary: Donna Regina 是来自德国的二人组合，《Follow The Sea》是他们签约 Karaoke Kalk 厂牌前的代表作，将电子流行与异域风情、dub、lounge 音乐混合，定位在 Julee Cruise 与 Saint Etienne 之间的模糊地带。女主唱 Regina 的声音清澈精准，男搭档 Günther Janssen 的合成器编排受 Kraftwerk 影响，在长曲中铺陈出极简的电子结构，并巧妙采样 Aphex Twin 的素材。专辑风格跨度颇大，从 dub 味的美式公路感一路延伸到碎拍节奏与仪式感打击乐实验，但所有元素始终保持着统一的低调节制气质，没有过度炫技。这种克制的文学性流行在当下已极为少见，两位音乐人自 1992 年起持续创作，音乐中流淌着对各类型音乐的热爱与研究痕迹。

items.body:
Bureau B compile stray new wave and NDW-adjacent bullets by overlooked ‘80s Austrian, Swiss, and German artists, including many making their first legit appearance.

The spiky drive and romantic melodies of early-mid ’80s Mittel European dancefloors is fully embraced on ‘Sowas von Egal 3 (German Synth Wave Underground 1981-86)’ with some 16 nuggets sifted from tape compilations and hard-to-find pressings. Prevailing streams of US & UK new wave, disco and punk are puckered with a Teutonic efficiency and wizzed-up sexiness on all counts from the bubbling hook of ‘He Sabine’ by Guyer’s Connection’ thru the DAF-esque swag of an EBM pioneer Tommi Stumpf in ‘Contergan Punk’, taking in proper club gems in Starter’s ‘Night By Night (7” Version)’, a bit of Talking Heads-like punk-funk-NDW on ‘Almenrausch’ and even Bliondie nod on ‘Die Shadocks’ ‘Disco-Liebe’. There’s some weirder robe-disco a la Felix Kubin in ‘Geduld’ by Ziggy & Eno, and a class slice of goth-rock in X-Beliebig’s ‘Morgen’.
items._genre: synth wave / NDW / EBM / new wave / darkwave
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑由Bureau B厂牌策划，精选1981至86年间德语区（德国、奥地利、瑞士）被忽视的地下音乐人作品，共收录16首曲目，多数为首次正式发行。整体风格融合了德式新浪潮的尖锐节奏与浪漫旋律，合成器驱动的舞曲质感贯穿始终。选曲涵盖多种方向：Guyer’s Connection的泡泡感流行钩子、Tommi Stumpf带有DAF气质的EBM强硬律动、Starter的俱乐部金曲、Ziggy & Eno受Felix Kubin启发的怪诞迪斯科，以及X-Beliebig的哥特摇滚。整张合辑呈现的是德语区在80年代英美新浪潮影响下发展出的独特变体，虽非高度实验性作品，但对了解这一时期中欧地下电子场景具有史料价值。

items.body:
A second pressing of last year’s gorgeous fourth and final album from Old Saw, the American Primitive project of Tongue Depressor's Henry Birdsey, riffing on the classic Takoma paradigm with additional ferric washes and layered instrumental drones, huge recommendation if yr into Bruce Langhorne’s ‘The Hired Hand’ or classic work by Daniel Lanois, Laraaji, Pelt, Stars Of The Lid, State River Widening.

'The Wringing Cloth' is Birdsey’s fourth and final Old Saw outing, and ironically it’s also the one that has garnered most amount of critical and commercial success. Old Saw’s shimmering, drone-heavy soundscapes were recorded on 1/4" tape at various locations in New England over the last few years and are once again paired with evocative black and white imagery from photographer Dylan Hausthor, whose landscapes somehow perfectly capture the timeless, widescreen appeal of the music inside.

Birdsey's pedal, lap steel and resonator are at the core of each track, but the album also features Old Saw’s usual personnel; Harper Reed on nylon string guitar and banjo, Ira Dorset on fiddle and bowed strings, Ann Rowlis on reed organ and harmonium, Jim Cutler on telecaster, Addison Starkweather-Price on bass, and Peter Catchpole on metal objects and power hammer. That lap steel lends the music its stylistic anchor, taking us through decades of American folk before gently fraying at the edges. Birdsey's application of classical minimalism - the themes that surge through his work with Zach Rowden as Tongue Depressor - is still somehow present here, especially as the record pulls into its second side and the shimmering country-fied atmosphere is pierced with bell-like sounds, but the overall mood and flavour of the record is distinctly easy on the ear and timeless in its appeal.

As the label put it, “What has always been uncanny about this music is that it arrives in a state at once familiar and obscured, like a memory weighed down with sensory information but no identifying details to place it. The Wringing Cloth walks off further into that geographical dream without time or language, until it’s just a speck of light….”
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由Tongue Depressor成员Henry Birdsey的Old Saw项目录制，使用四分之一英寸磁带在新英格兰各地完成录音。乐器编制以踏板滑棒吉他、膝上钢棒和共鸣器为核心，辅以尼龙弦吉他、班卓琴、小提琴、簧风琴与电吉他等。整张唱片延续美式原始吉他传统，但融入了分层器乐嗡鸣与磁带噪音质感，将古典极简主义的结构逻辑嵌入美国民间音乐脉络中。录音强调空间感与时间的模糊性，嗡鸣氛围层叠展开，铃铛般音色在第二面逐渐浮现，与黑白摄影形成视听呼应。磁带介质的温暖失真与器乐长线条构建出一种熟悉却又难以定位的地理梦境，适合偏爱跨类型融合的听众。

items.body:
More Mark & Moritz worship gang, this time with a strong paean to the Main Street series, featuring vocals from Prince Morella doing his best Paul St. Hilaire = good stuff.

With some added Titonton Duvanté-style stabs, it’s a pretty faithful, if marginally harder hitting, Round Two style heater, with a version included, plus a rework on the flip that kills the vox in favour of more atmosphere and thumping kicks.

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑是对经典Mark & Moritz路线及Main Street系列的致敬之作。Prince Morella的人声演绎带有Paul St. Hilaire的影子，慵懒而克制，Titonton Duvanté式的合成器刺音穿插其中，呈现出比Round Two更硬朗的质感。收录的版本保留了完整的人声与节拍骨架，而反面则将人声抽离，转向氛围营造与重击踢鼓，提供另一种聆听路径。对于熟悉底特律系深层律动与复古舞曲美学的听众而言，这是一张兼具怀旧指向与制作诚意的作品。整体定位清晰，执行忠实，但缺乏明显的突破性视野。

items.body:
Detroit affiliate Naoyaki Yamakawa (DJ Compufunk) with 2006 recordings as Lovegod for Richard Akingbehin’s Kynant Records, backed with Priori & Janeret remixes.

Joining the likes of Paul St. Hilaire, Vril, and Terence Dixon on the label, Osaka’s Lovegod pursues a classic deep 313 sound in ‘Rendezvous’, speaking to years of 12”s for likes of Motech and Yore with a fine grasp of Motor City techno-house romance, all whirring groove synched with fluttering arps and lushest pads. The remix by Canada’s Priori is faithful to the OG, but more streamlined, echoing vintage Convexton and Claude Young, whereas Janeret’s dub dials it down to a breezier stride.
items._genre: deep techno / detroit techno / house / deep house
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由大阪制作人Lovegod操刀，追随底特律经典深沉之声，在Kynant厂牌呈现。整张作品以旋转律动为核心，琶音如蝴蝶般轻盈翻飞，铺垫垫音色泽饱满，营造出浓厚的技术宅浪漫气息。Priori的混音版本更为简洁锐利，向Convexton与Claude Young的复古美学致敬；Janeret的dub混音则将节奏放缓，呈现更轻盈通透的律动感。整体走的是传统底特律技术与芝加哥浩室交融的路线，编曲扎实、情绪暧昧，虽非前卫实验之作，但对电子音乐爱好者而言仍是值得细品的精致产物。

items.body:
Capturing an in-situ rehearsal of The Sterling Jubilee Singers, a long-running African American a cappella quartet, 'Jesus Hits like the Atom Bomb' provides an intimate view of a dying folk tradition.

We should all know by now the foundational influence African American gospel music has had on subsequent popular forms, from country to house, but we rarely get to hear the real thing. This set was produced by the Alabama Folklife Association and aimed to document the rigorous process the Sterling Jubilees went through each week to maintain their notoriously high level of activity. The group was formed way back in 1929 from African American miners and mill workers in Birmingham, Alabama, and 'Jesus Hits...' catches up with them in 1994 in a hall that serendipitously sat next to a railway line. And whether you have any interest in OG gospel a cappella music or not, it's fascinating to hear the quartet in their element, praying in-between recreating their elaborate (and impeccably sung) set of standards. It's a porthole into another universe, for those of us who grew up far from the American South.
