items.body: Review by kev rowland — Formed in the early 80's by keyboard player Derk Akkermann, Saris have had different line-ups over the years combined with periods of inactivity. I enjoyed their last album, 2020's 'Beyond The Rainbow', but said there needed to be quite a few changes to be able to move ahead although I never thought they would have a total rethink of approach and alter the line-up but that is what has happened. Henrik Wager (lead & backing vocals) and Lutz G�nther (bass) are also still there, but they have now been joined by veteran proggers Jimmy Keegan (drums, percussion), Marek Arnold (saxophone) and Martin Schnella (guitars), which has changed their music in multiple ways, all for the better. More of a thematic album than a concept, it has been influenced by the state of the world, the power, the politics, the paranoia, religion and revenge, technology and temptation, corruption and contradiction. There is a need to save ourselves from others and sometime save others from ourselves, and for those of us living away from Europe, America or the Middle East, it sometimes we feel we are the only sane ones left and the world is tearing itself to pieces so I certainly understand where they are coming from.Musically this is symphonic prog combined with some prog metal, power ballads, stadium rock, melodic metal etc. Wager has a great voice, while any album which contains Schnella and Arnold will always be wonderfully arranged with many layers combining to produce something special, but in many ways this album belongs to Keegan. It is his drumming which drives through songs which may otherwise be a little bland and over-produced, creating an inventive framework for others to work around. I certainly hope this is a new band as opposed to the older members plus session musicians, as if this is what they produce the first time they are together I can't wait to see what they come up with next.The only real downside for me is a passage within "Mamucium" at the five-minute mark which is so heavily influenced by Genesis it could possibly be thought of as a "steal" from "Apocalypse in 9/8". That small point aside, this is a thoroughly enjoyable release which is easy to listen to with good hooks, wonderful vocals, and melodies. And did I mention the drumming? This is a real step up from the last album.
items._cn_summary: SARIS Project 2026年专辑《Off World》由键盘手Derk Akkermann在八十年代初组建的乐队经历重大阵容重组而成，加入鼓手Jimmy Keegan、萨克斯手Marek Arnold和吉他手Martin Schnella等资深前卫音乐人。专辑以主题而非概念形式构建，围绕世界政治、技术诱惑、宗教矛盾等议题展开。音乐融合交响前卫、力量金属、抒情摇滚和旋律金属等多种风格，编曲层次丰富，Keegan的鼓点成为推动力。整体偏向传统欧式前卫摇滚路线，Genesis影响明显，部分段落被指有借鉴之嫌。专辑制作精良，旋律抓耳，人声出色，但对追求实验性、爵士即兴或电子融合的听众而言，跨界探索有限，基本停留在类型框架内的演进。

items.body: Review by Sean Trane — Add another halstar really!!!A weird exploitation product that features two very different eras of the Gillan/Glover line-up.TBH, I don't find much interest in the 72 Paris Theatre concert on the second disc, since most of itis +/- the same than in the Made In Japan double live disc. But the first disc (early 1970 in BBC studios) is an essential, but very imperfect, showing how theMk2 line-up had to deal with the MK1 era material, since they hadn't developed enough material toaccompany their fresj In Rock release. Speed King and Child In Time are the two emblematic tracksfrom their new album, but most of the interest comes from the two elongated tracks from theirTaliesin album. Both Mabrake Rooy and Wring That Neck are jam & improv infested tracks, not alwaysof great interest (Blackmore going Classical is much less convincing than Lord going classical), asthey sometimes err in order to gain time. Nevertheless, both tracks are a joy to hear under thenewqsuintet, and that's what matters. I would've definitely liked to hear more og the G&G pairindulge" in more E&S era stuff.
items._cn_summary: 这张现场专辑收录了深紫乐队两个不同时期的演出。1972年巴黎剧院的演出内容与经典现场专辑《Made In Japan》重复度较高，价值有限。1970年BBC录音棚的演出则展示了第二期阵容演绎第一期作品的过渡阶段，乐队当时尚未积累足够的原创曲目来配合新专辑《In Rock》的发行。《Speed King》和《Child In Time》作为新专辑代表曲出现，而更值得关注的是来自《Taliesin》专辑的两首长曲——《Mabrake Rooy》和《Wring That Neck》，充满即兴延伸和自由jam元素，但部分段落被认为是为了争取时间而显得拖沓。评论者认为布莱克摩尔的古典化处理不如洛德的古典化尝试令人信服，但五重奏的新鲜诠释仍具聆听价值。

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — 2026 sees the release of Muse's most relevant and diverse studio album in about two decades or so.'The Wow! Signal' is the tenth full-length studio recording from the British alternative rockdarlings and sees them bringing in producer Dan Lancaster for the first time around. Pushing thetrio to pursuit a more modern production, Lancaster definitely influenced the sound of this record,which exhibits certain similarities to other alternative bands like Bring Me the Horizon and ThreeDays Grace, with which Lancaster has also worked throughout the years. Thematically, 'The Wow!Signal' deals with space and cosmic mysteries, while some songs definitely feel like more personalstatements from Mat Bellamy. Calling this album "space rock" would then be inaccurate because itexhibits elements of alternative rock, art pop and electronic music, offering some truly proggyriffs and several unorthodox arrangements. 'The Wow! Signal' is a more of a typical maximalist Museventure that impresses with an overt-the-top energy and stunning production all throughout.In the light of this consideration, it is very interesting to hear all the different styles the bandcovers on this album. Opening their set with the unbridled and anthemic piece 'The Dark Forest', animmediate wave of nostalgic Muse pretentiousness overwhelms the listener with orchestralarrangements, anxious falsettos, and muscular guitar riffs. This is followed by 'NightshiftSuperstar', one of the most convincing singles released by the band in recent years, and anexcellent song that echoes the dance-pop aesthetic of Muse's last two albums. 'Cryogen' is anotherinteresting song that combines the art rock dynamics of earlier Muse with a futuristic electronicsound that once again reminisces the output of other contemporary alt-rock/metal acts. Later on weget 'Hexagons', which sounds like a sophisticated prog-pop number, and while it could have feltcompletely out of place on this album, the final result is actually impressive. Perhaps the mostenjoyable parts of 'The Wow! Signal' are the ones where Muse explore a darker alt-metal sound andthe tracks 'The Sickness in You & I' and 'Unravelling' are definitely fine examples. The EllieGoulding feature on 'Hush' is quite intriguing as well, as this duet actually turns out to be a veryenjoyable and unexpected entry!All in all, 'The Wow! Signal' achieves an excellent balance between modern production and nostalgicMuse maximalism. The arrangements, vocals, and overall instrumentation on this album are top-notch,and the entire thing feels like a coherent sonically intense work. On top of that, the trio deliverssome of their most compelling songs as of late. Excellent return to form from Muse!
items._genre: alternative rock / art pop / electronic / progressive rock
items._cn_summary: 这是英国乐队Muse的第十张录音室专辑，由新制作人Dan Lancaster操刀，呈现出比以往更现代的音色质感。专辑主题围绕太空与宇宙之谜展开，融合另类摇滚、艺术流行与电子音乐元素，管弦乐编排、假声演唱与厚重吉他riff交替出现。曲目如《The Dark Forest》以宏大编曲开场，《Nightshift Superstar》偏向舞曲流行，《Hexagons》呈现复杂的进步流行结构，《The Sickness in You & I》与《Unravelling》则探索更暗色调的另类金属领域。《Hush》邀请Ellie Goulding对唱，形成意外亮点。整体制作精良，乐队在现代音色与自身华丽摇滚传统之间取得了平衡，但本质上仍是一张制作考究的主流另类摇滚作品。

items.body: Rexx Arkana, the New York DJ, producer and vocalist who co-founded the harsh EBM act FGFC820 and led the cancer-charity project Bruderschaft, has died on July 3rd, 2026 after a long battle with cancer. He was 57. Born Rik Millhouse, he had beaten thyroid cancer in 2015 but was diagnosed with a new Stage 4 cancer in the summer of 2025. He left hospital on June 29th to spend the little time he still had left with his family. Side-Line extends its sincere condolences to his family, friends and collaborators. Rexx Arkana, a DJ and organiser at the centre of the US scene Arkana worked at the centre of the North American dark-electronic community for close to four decades. He began DJing on Syracuse University radio in 1987 and went on to spin industrial, EBM and synth music across the United States and beyond, taking his stage name from Ministry’s Al Jourgensen. Away from the decks he wrote and edited, serving as managing editor of the magazine “Interface”, and he built the video series Statik Industrial Television, a filmed diary of North American dark-electronic events. Side-Line covered that launch when Arkana set up the Statik Industrial TV channel in 2018. He remained closely tied to VampireFreaks and its Dark Force Fest, and ran his own Haus Arkana imprint. FGFC820 and harsh EBM Rexx Arkana co-founded FGFC820 in New York in 2004 with fellow DJ Dräcos. The duo built a harsh EBM sound around blunt beats, hard synth lines and Arkana’s shouted vocals, and released mainly through the German label NoiTekk, with US editions on COP International. Their catalogue runs from the debut EP “The Hanging Garden” (2005) through the albums “Urban Audio Warfare” (2006), “Law & Ordnance” (2008) and “Homeland Insecurity” (2012), followed by the “American History Vol. 1” compilation on Haus Arkana in 2022. FGFC820 played festivals including Wave-Gotik-Treffen in Leipzig and Kinetik in Montreal, and appeared on Alfa Matrix’s “Endzeit Bunkertracks” series. Bruderschaft and ‘Forever’ Bruderschaft was Rexx Arkana’s charity project, and it carried a personal history. He wrote the lyrics for “Forever” after his father, Charles Richard Millhouse, died of cancer in 1999, also at the age of 57, and dedicated the release to him. The 2003 single, out via Alfa Matrix in Europe, drew together a cast from across the scene: Ronan Harris of VNV Nation on vocals, Sebastian Komor of Icon of Coil on production, Joakim Montelius of Covenant on samples and Stephan Groth of Apoptygma Berzerk on backing vocals, with a remix set from Front 242, Camouflage, Feindflug, Melotron and others. “Forever” reached number one on the German Alternative Charts, and Bruderschaft directed its proceeds to cancer charities, raising close to 50,000 dollars across the project. You can hear “Forever” through the Bandcamp player below. Forever by Bruderschaft Bruderschaft returned a decade later with the album “Return”, again released by Alfa Matrix on 22 November 2013, and again as a benefit record. The nine-song album added another line-up of guest singers, among them Tom Shear of Assemblage 23, Daniel Graves of Aesthetic Perfection, Daniel Myer of Haujobb and Clint Carney of System Syn. The first edition shipped in a carton box with a bonus disc of remixes. A long connection to Side-Line and Alfa Matrix Rexx Arkana’s work reached Side-Line and Alfa Matrix directly. Bruderschaft released both “Forever” and “Return” through Alfa Matrix and kept its catalogue on the label, and FGFC820 featured on Alfa Matrix compilations. Rexx was also a contributor to Side-Line and at a certain moment had his own article series in 2013, called 80sObscurities. Originally started as a Facebook community showcasing forgotten retro electronic tracks, Rexx Arkana’s prose and music curation were later syndicated directly by Side-Line Magazine. At Side-Line we also reported on the health of Rexx Arkana, for instance when the community rallied around him after he was first diagnosed with cancer in the mid-2010s, and in the background raised funds. That a musician who built a project to fund cancer research would later face the disease himself, and fight it publicly with the support of his wife and daughters, was not lost on those who knew him. Tributes came quickly. Empathy Test frontman Isaac Howlett recalled Arkana reaching out early in his band’s career for an interview in London on behalf of the site I Die You Die, and described him as “a powerhouse of energy, enthusiasm and community spirit” who “always gave more than he took.” On a personal note: just before Alfa Matrix launched the Bruderschaft project, Rexx Arkana stayed at my flat in Leuven for two weeks while working in Brussels for his day job. I got to know him as an extremely productive and gentle person (and I got to know very well his remix skills, for instance when he mixed Britney Spears and VNV Nation together). It saddens me deeply that Rexx Arkana has lost his battle with cancer. Only a few people leave a lasting legacy in this scene, and he is surely one of them. Farewell, my friend. And to quote Rexx: “If you love someone, every day is a chance to prove it. Your chances aren’t infinite, so please don’t lose any.”
items._cn_summary: 本文为悼念性质的新闻报道，纪念已故纽约DJ与制作人Rexx Arkana，介绍其在北美洲暗黑电子音乐场景中近四十年的DJ活动、杂志编辑及影视制作经历。文章重点回顾他与Dräcos于2004年共同创立的硬核EBM项目FGFC820的唱片目录与演出履历，涵盖从首张EP到四张专辑的发行脉络。该项目主要通过德国厂牌NoiTekk和COP International发行。此外还详述其慈善项目Bruderschaft的2003年单曲《Forever》，该曲汇聚了VNV Nation、Icon of Coil、Covenant、Apoptygma Berzerk等艺人参与，曾登上德国另类榜单首位，并将收益捐予癌症慈善机构。文章未涉及任何具体音乐分析或评论性内容。

items.body: Melbourne four-piece Karate Boogaloo wrote “Booger’s Bounce of Joy” for a dance they kept seeing at their gigs. There are no steps to it: you move every limb however you want. Callum Riley‘s organ runs the track with a growling tone, and underneath, Henry Jenkins‘s bass keeps a loose, summery groove for dancing. They recorded it live to tape with no overdubs, all four playing at once, keeping the focus entirely on a clear, hummable hook. Alongside Jenkins and Riley, percussionist and drummer Hudson Whitlock and guitarist Darvid Thor complete the quartet, the same four who play the rhythm section in Melbourne soul band The Cactus Channel. Under their own name they play instrumental funk on drums, guitar, bass and organ, a small-combo sound they take from The Meters and Booker T. & The MG’s. The four have worked Melbourne’s instrumental soul scene for over a decade: the KB’s Mixtape series came first, funk reworkings of hip-hop samples that sold out local record shops on word of mouth, and 2024’s Hold Your Horses gave them a second album of originals. They cut “Booger’s Bounce of Joy” with engineer Alex Bennett at Sound Recordings, running it through their Ampex 440 tape machine. The single comes ahead of Access All Areas, their new album for Colemine Records and College of Knowledge Records. Stream “Booger’s Bounce of Joy” HERE and pre-order Access All Areas via THIS LINK. The post Daily Discovery: Karate Boogaloo – Booger’s Bounce of Joy appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._genre: instrumental funk / soul jazz / retro groove
items._cn_summary: Karate Boogaloo 是来自墨尔本的四件乐队，由风琴手 Callum Riley、贝斯手 Henry Jenkins、鼓手 Hudson Whitlock 和吉他手 Darvid Thor 组成，他们同时也是灵魂乐队 The Cactus Channel 的节奏声部。这首《Booger's Bounce of Joy》是为现场观众中自发展开的一种即兴舞蹈而创作的——没有固定舞步，自由摆动四肢。整曲以 Riley 的咆哮风琴为主导音色，Jenkins 的贝斯在底部撑起松散而夏日感的律动。四人同期录音至磁带，无后期叠加，专注于一条清晰易记的钩子旋律。他们深受 The Meters 和 Booker T. & The MG's 的小编制声响美学影响，制作经由 Ampex 440 磁带机完成。此曲作为新专辑《Access All Areas》的先行单曲发行，由 Colemine Records 和 College of Knowledge Records 联合出品。整篇文章实质上是新单曲与专辑的宣传新闻稿，缺乏深度乐评内容。

items.tags: 邦楽 邦楽ポップ／ロック 映画／映像 邦楽 書籍 書籍 Number_i 神宮寺勇太 平野紫耀 岸優太
items.excerpt: Number_iが、新曲“BUGS LIFE”を2026年7月13日（月）にデジタルリリースする。 神宮寺勇太がプロデュースを務めた同楽曲は、デジタル音像をキーとして〈デジタルというものは何か〉というテーマを紐解いていくことから制作がスタートした。自分たちがファンの前で歌っている奇跡的な状況や、いくつもの偶然が重なり合って現在があることをシステムにおける一瞬の〈バグ〉に例え、そこから着想を得て歌詞の世界観を作っていったという。 楽曲のベースとなるジャンルには、激しいサウンドが特徴のフォンクを採用。通常のフォンク特有の速いBPMをあえて抑えめに設定し、Number_iの魅力である〈ダンス〉をしっかりと魅せる構成となっている。随所にアフリカンビートやラテンビートを取り入れ、Number_iらしい、いきなりビートが切り替わるスリリングな展開にも注目だ。 なお、アスキーアートを使用した“BUGS LIFE”のティザー動画も公開されたほか、楽曲の世界観に合わせた新たなアーティスト写真も解禁されている。

items.body:
Balinese gamelan master Dewa Alit's third Black Truffle outing, 'Baur Bentur' continues to shake up the formula like it's a margarita, placing Alit's Gamelan Salukat ensemble alongside virtuoso jazz pianist Sri Hanuraga.

With each of Alit's Black Truffle albums, his first releases outside of Indonesia, the performer, composer, instrument designer and bandleader has projected Balinese gamelan forms into bold new places. 2020's 'Genetic' set the scene, introducing his orchestra and his uniquely tuned scale and its follow-up, 2022's 'Chasing the Phantom' considered gamelan's immense influence on electronic music, centering some of Alit's most experimental material. On 'Baur Bentur', which means "mixing and smashing", Alit again looks at the push-and-pull between East and West, this time wondering how to work out a fusion that's progressive, not something formulated around the gaze of parasitic tourists. He invites Jakarta-born Hanuraga to help him realize this goal and its a sensible choice; considered one of Indonesia's most talented young pianists, Hanuraga understands both avant-garde jazz and traditional Indonesian music implicitly. 

His playing is measured but ornate on 'Sukat Tacara', played in fast flurries of notes that recall gamelan without mimicking the form. It allows Alit's ensemble to take a different approach, laying down hollow rhythms at first and slow chimes before speeding up into more traditional overlayed, lightning-fast tones in the middle section. And it's at this moment that Hanuraga really steps into the spotlight, playing jerky Thelonius Monk-style sequences that mutate seamlessly into cascading gamelan riffs. The title track on the flip takes a different approach again, integrating Hanuraga's piano more holistically into the ensemble, where it follows the gamelan's rhythmelodic thrust absolutely, adding emphasis, accent and intrigue to a sound that's already exceptionally singular.

items.body: Take my hand, Let me show you how the night runs out Denver’s Devoratus make darkwave with a clenched jaw and a dancer’s thrust, and Vacio, their EP whose title translates from Spanish as “Empty” or “Void,” turns that tension into a lean, bruised little machine. The current lineup—Tomas on vocals, Aero on synths, Renee on bass, and Cisco adding live guitar—works from familiar gothic materials, yet the record has a focused personality: dry humour at the edge of despair, Spanish-language ache beside English plainspokenness, and club velocity pressed against private collapse. The production favors cold angles and thick low end. Synth parts hang in the air like metal under moonlight, while Renee’s bass gives each track a stalking physicality. Aero’s keys cut through with glassy discipline, sometimes framing the beat, sometimes needling it, while the guitar’s presence traces the shadows into a sharper human shape. Tomas sings as if addressing someone across a locked room, his voice grave, close, and melancholic, carrying the EP’s themes of isolation, desire, mortality, and change without turning them into costume drama or diary theater. Abismo oscuro comes out of the gate with an icy guitar line, cold synths settling over it like a layer of winter frost. The drumming pushes forward with almost punk impatience, while the shadowy vocal line rides the rush with a sense of momentum, doom, and romantic wreckage that recalls Lowlife at their darkest. Lyrically, the song stares straight into death’s mirror: sin is abandoned, the cross is taken up, the end is declared present, and the body is returned to dust. Its devotional language and blunt mortality give the track a ritual severity, less like melodrama than an alarm bell ringing in a freezing room. The song moves fast without losing its shape, giving its gloom a sharp edge rather than letting it dissolve into decorative fog. It lands with urgency, not clutter. Dance is the release’s most direct invitation to the floor, though its pleasure has a sickly grin. Echoed vocals stretch across atmospheric synths, and the rhythm keeps the body busy while the mind wanders toward less friendly rooms. The lyrics turn the dance floor into both seduction and survival: the Spanish lines suggest instruction, surrender, and a refusal to look back, while the English refrain reaches outward like a hand in the dark. It is not escapism exactly, but movement as a last practical response to ruin. Dance music can carry dread without collapsing into theatre; Devoratus understand that the best grooves can feel useful, almost medicinal, as if motion itself were the only thing keeping the void from closing in. For You keeps the tempo high but aims closer to the chest. It plays as a fast ballad for someone already gone or maybe still too near, with echo, ache, and forward drive braided into a clean blow. The narrator wakes disoriented, caught in the repetition of not knowing where they are, unable to stop living inside the self. When the song turns toward Spanish, that private confusion becomes a plea for an ending and a way out, not simply for escape, but for another person. That shift gives the track its emotional weight. It is wounded without becoming helpless, romantic without becoming soft. The restraint gives the record leverage: Devoratus leave enough space around the parts, so every bass note, drum hit, guitar slash, and vocal bend lands with intention. Vacio is compact, stylish, and severe, yet it breathes. Its emptiness is not blankness, but pressure: the absence one dances through, prays against, wakes inside, and tries to outrun. Fans of Forever Grey, Lebanon Hanover, She Past Away, and other cold-hearted romantics will recognize the alleyways it traverses, but Devoratus walk them with their own private map. This is gothic dance music with bite, brains, and bleak charge for rooms already leaning toward the dark. items.body: One Must Forget, the post-industrial project of Polish musician Michał Kiełbasa and vocalist EA, have released their debut album “Pillars of Shame” through the German label Ant-Zen. The record came out digitally on 18 June 2026 and arrives on a limited vinyl edition of 100 copies. The duo describe their sound as “angstpop”, a cold, minimal strain of industrial built on hardware and analog decay. You can stream “Pillars of Shame” and order the vinyl through the Bandcamp player below. Pillars of Shame by One Must Forget One Must Forget detail ‘Pillars of Shame’ One Must Forget pair Kiełbasa’s hardware-based industrial with the vocals of EA, credited only as an enigmatic female vocalist. The album balances stripped-back minimalism with heavier machine rhythms, feedback and white noise, set against slower melodic passages. Kiełbasa recorded, produced, mixed and mastered the record at Antisound Studio in Tarnowskie Góry in 2025, and Ant-Zen founder Stefan Alt handled the artwork. The digital album runs to twelve tracks: “Above an Emptiness”, “Suffering Engaged”, “Light without Me”, “Pillars of Shame”, “From a Person to Nothing”, “Grief Design”, “Nature of Mankind”, “Hate”, “Guilt”, “Choose My Own Death”, “Under the Water” and “To the Point of Tears”. The 100-copy vinyl pressing carries ten of the twelve tracks, on black vinyl in a matte black die-cut sleeve with a digital download code. About One Must Forget One Must Forget is a Polish and French project fronted by Michał Kiełbasa, who also records as Neithan and works out of Tarnowskie Góry in southern Poland. Kiełbasa is active across several projects: Whalesong, the experimental band he formed in 2009 that mixes sludge, doom, noise rock and post-punk; Lugola, his noise and power-electronics solo project started in 2012; and Harmony of Struggle, a power-electronics project he founded in 2020. “Pillars of Shame” is the debut release under the One Must Forget name, made with vocalist EA. Ant-Zen, which releases the album, is a German label founded in 1994 by Stefan Alt, its name derived from “Anti Zensur”. The label has documented industrial, rhythmic noise, power electronics and ambient for three decades. “Pillars of Shame” adds One Must Forget to that catalogue as a debut, and the limited vinyl run keeps the release in line with Ant-Zen’s small-batch physical editions.
